- DefinitionsHTML: <section class="pos-block"><div class="pos-title">adjective <span class="pron">/ˌɑːtɪˈfɪʃəl◂/</span></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">1</span><div class="phrase">NATURAL 1</div><div class="activator">ARTIFICIAL</div><div class="def-en">not real or not made of natural things but made to be like something that is real or natural</div><div class="def-cn">人造的，人工的</div><div class="relations">SYN false · OPP natural</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">artificial flowers</div><div class="example-cn">假花</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">artificial light</div><div class="example-cn">人造光</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">artificial fertilizers</div><div class="example-cn">化肥</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">2</span><div class="def-en">an artificial situation or quality exists because someone has made it exist, and not because it is really necessary</div><div class="def-cn">人为的</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">artificial distinctions</div><div class="example-cn">人为差别</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">artificial barriers of gender and race</div><div class="example-cn">性别和种族的人为障碍</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">3</span><div class="activator">PRETEND</div><div class="def-en">artificial behaviour is not sincere – used to show disapproval</div><div class="def-cn">〔行为〕虚假的，不真挚的，矫揉造作的〔含贬义〕</div><div class="relations">OPP genuine</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">an artificial smile</div><div class="example-cn">假笑</div></div></div></section>
- CorpusHTML: <section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">artificial</div><ul><li>On the surface she seems quite a pleasant woman, but there&#x27;s something very artificial about her.</li><li>High import taxes give their goods an artificial advantage in the market.</li><li>Carter was saying all the right things, but his smile was artificial, and I knew I couldn&#x27;t trust him.</li><li>The natural and artificial characterizing ingredients must be named on the labels.</li><li>artificial Christmas trees</li><li>In front of the grate was a tall electric fire with artificial coals, a high curved back and a triple set of burners.</li><li>The juice contains no artificial coloring or flavors.</li><li>Our ice cream contains no artificial colors or flavors.</li><li>Paradoxically the ecological problems deriving from the application of artificial fertilizers are often equally complex and extensive.</li><li>On the table was a vase filled with artificial flowers.</li><li>Through binoculars I had noted the breakwaters of what appeared to be a small artificial harbour just a mile along the coast.</li><li>Constraint-based programming is an artificial intelligence technique which finds the optimum way to allocate means and resources.</li><li>Glen wears an artificial leg.</li><li>It took Frank a while to learn to walk with the artificial leg.</li><li>The plants can grow just as well in artificial light.</li><li>We have one of those electric heaters with artificial logs.</li><li>A wreath of artificial poppies has been held down by a brick.</li><li>I usually use artificial sweetener in my coffee instead of sugar.</li><li>artificial sweeteners for coffee</li><li>An example, perhaps slightly artificial, would be found in a family photograph.</li></ul></section>
- OriginHTML: <div class="origin">artificial (1300-1400) Old French artificiel, from Latin artificialis, from artificium; → ARTIFICE</div>

- DefinitionsHTML: <section class="pos-block"><div class="pos-title">preposition <span class="pron">/bɪˈsaɪd/</span></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">1</span><div class="activator">NEXT don’t look very good beside last year’s results.</div><div class="example-cn">今年的销售额和去年相比不是很好。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">The children seemed tiny beside him.</div><div class="example-cn">孩子们在他身边显得只有一丁点大。</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">3</span><div class="phrase">be beside yourself</div><div class="activator">ANGRY</div><div class="def-en">to be feeling so angry, excited etc that you find it difficult to control yourself</div><div class="def-cn">〔由于气愤、激动等而〕失去控制；忘形</div><div class="patterns"><span class="example-cn">那个可怜的女孩快要气疯了。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">Mom and Dad will be beside themselves with worry.</div><div class="example-cn">爸爸和妈妈会担心死的。</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">4</span><div class="phrase">be beside the point</div><div class="activator">CONNECTED WITH</div><div class="def-en">to not be directly connected with the main subject or problem that you are talking about</div><div class="def-cn">离题，与主题无关</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">He’s very - CorpusHTML: <section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">be beside yourself</div><ul><li>I thought it was outrageous, and Clarisa was beside herself.</li><li>I was beside myself with joy and excitement.</li><li>Many observers believe that Kiley and Livingstone should be beside themselves with joy at the major concessions they have won.</li><li>She was beside herself with grief.</li><li>The boy was beside himself with agitation.</li><li>They had been publicly assaulted and humiliated in front of a crowd of people and were beside themselves with rage.</li><li>When he found that his theory exactly predicted the path of Mercury, he was beside himself with happiness for days.</li><li>When the Republicans tried to eliminate some of the things I felt proudest about, I was beside myself about it.</li></ul></section><section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">be beside the point</div><ul><li>It&#x27;s unrealistic, but that&#x27;s beside the point - it&#x27;s just good entertainment.</li><li>But the pedigree of this idea is beside the point.</li><li>But to criticize Mr Hall&#x27;s production as an exercise in fuddy-duddy Shakespeare is beside the point.</li><li>He may manufacture these life units as required and he may simply have a given supply: that is beside the point.</li><li>She had come to no harm, but that was beside the point.</li><li>This semantic distinction is beside the point; the special admissions program is undeniably a classification based on race and ethnic back-ground.</li><li>What the outcome of seeing him might be is beside the point.</li></ul></section><section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">beside</div><ul><li>Delhi is so old that many European cities actually look young beside it.</li><li>Tom&#x27;s efforts seemed so weak beside Martin&#x27;s.</li><li>Ella came and sat down beside me.</li><li>Gary, come sit beside me.</li><li>On the table beside the bed were several medicine bottles.</li><li>The loss of the port pales beside the gain of a peace treaty.</li><li>a cabin beside the lake</li><li>They were sitting beside the pool, eating breakfast.</li></ul></section><section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">right beside</div><ul><li>It was pumping from something right beside her, pooling around her legs.</li><li>Cardiff froze in his tracks, and now the others were right beside him; all staring back at this impossible sight.</li><li>A lighted taper appeared in mid-air, right beside him.</li><li>Lincoln stayed right beside me, pressing against me as I yanked on the car door, having trouble getting it open.</li><li>And Miguel would be sitting right beside Spider, like his old lieutenant.</li><li>Turn right beside the stream to junction with main river.</li><li>And right beside them were graduates from Yale, Stanford, and Penn.</li></ul></section>

region.</li><li>The drug squad&#x27;s briefing lasted twenty minutes.</li><li>Would a seasoned brief have lost it in court so easily?</li><li>The brief given to the students was quite straightforward.</li><li>The brief comprised a list of about 80 species for each chart, grouped according to pollution tolerance.</li><li>For all but the simplest actions there should preferably be a written brief which is discussed by all concerned.</li></ul></section><section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">brief</div><ul><li>The client should then be briefed.</li><li>It was clear the witness had been well briefed.</li><li>DeGaulle flew back to England to be briefed about the invasion that was about to begin.</li><li>A reporter who attempted to cover the meeting was asked to leave but was briefed afterward by project officials on what happened.</li><li>Police officers were briefed before going out to arrest the suspects.</li><li>Barristers may not be approached directly by most clients: they may only be briefed by solicitors.</li><li>At Question Time the Prime Minister is backed by the civil servants who brief her and try to anticipate supplementary questions.</li><li>Make sure that the PR department are fully briefed on their role.</li><li>All teachers were personally briefed on this procedure, which is designed to minimise underreporting of smoking behaviour.</li><li>You&#x27;ll be picked up from here tomorrow night and briefed on what you have to do.</li><li>However, they have not been briefed that in this case the drop zone will be changed at the last minute.</li></ul></section><section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">brief somebody on something</div><ul><li>Congress has been fully briefed on the current situation in Haiti.</li></ul></section>

- DefinitionsHTML: <section class="pos-block"><div class="pos-title">verb <span class="homnum">1</span> <span class="pron">/siːs/</span></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">1</span><div class="phrase">stop</div><div class="register">formal</div><div class="activator">STOP DOING something · STOP HAPPENING</div><div class="def-en">to stop doing something or stop happening</div><div class="def-cn">停止，终止，结束</div><div class="patterns"><span class="label">Pattern</span> cease trading/production/operations etc · cease fire!</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">He ceased to be a member of the association.</div><div class="example-cn">他不再是该协会的会员。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">The things people will do for charity never cease to amaze me (= I am always surprised by them).</div><div class="example-cn">人们的慈善义举总是让我感到惊讶。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">the decision to cease using CFCs in packaging</div><div class="example-cn">停止在包装材料中使用氯氟烃的决定</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">The rain ceased and the sky cleared.</div><div class="example-cn">雨过天晴。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">The company ceased production at their Norwich plant last year.</div><div class="example-cn">去年该公司在诺里奇的工厂停止了生产。</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">2</span><div class="phrase">cease and desist</div><div class="register">law</div><div class="def-en">to stop doing something</div><div class="def-cn">终止及停止</div></div></section><section class="pos-block"><div class="pos-title">noun <span class="homnum">2</span></div><div class="sense"><div class="phrase">without cease</div><div class="register">formal</div><div class="activator">CONTINUOUS</div><div class="def-en">without stopping</div><div class="def-cn">不停地，持续地</div></div></section>
- UsageHTML: <section class="usage-box"><div class="usage-title">Register</div><div class="usage-en">In everyday English, people usually use stop rather than cease:</div><div class="usage-cn">在日常英语中，人们一般使用 stop ，而不用 cease</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">They have stopped using CFCs in packaging.</div><div class="example-cn">他们已经停止在包装材料中使用氯氟烃。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">The rain stopped just as the fireworks began.</div><div class="example-cn">烟火表演开始的时候雨正好停了。</div></div></section>

What a coincidence -- we were just talking about you.</li><li>My mother is called Anna, and by coincidence my wife&#x27;s mother is called Anna too.</li><li>We were all linked in a vast and rhythmic coincidence, a daisy chain of rumor, suspicion and secret wish.</li><li>By a strange coincidence the king was assassinated on the very spot where his grandfather had been killed.</li><li>After all, the coincidence could not be expected to occur so neatly every 150 million years.</li><li>It is regarded as a purely natural phenomenon which, by an unusual coincidence, occurs in the walls of their convent.</li></ul></section><section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">What a coincidence</div><ul><li>&quot;Ruby&#x27;s dad gave her the exact same thing that she gave us for our wedding.&quot; &quot;You&#x27;re kidding! What a coincidence.&quot;</li></ul></section><section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">coincidence of</div><ul><li>There is a coincidence of opinion among the board members.</li></ul></section>

- DefinitionsHTML: <section class="pos-block"><div class="pos-title">noun <span class="pron">/kənˈsepʃən/</span></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">1</span><div class="grammar">[countable C, uncountable U]</div><div class="activator">IDEA</div><div class="def-en">an idea about what something is like, or a general understanding of something</div><div class="def-cn">概念；观念，思想；想法</div><div class="patterns"><span class="label">Pattern</span> conception of</div><div class="relations">→ concept</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">the conception of parliamentary democracy</div><div class="example-cn">议会民主的概念</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">changing conceptions of the world</div><div class="example-cn">这个世界不断变化的观念</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">They have no conception of what women really feel and want.</div><div class="example-cn">他们对女性真正的感受和需求一无所知。</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">2</span><div class="grammar">[uncountable U]</div><div class="activator">INVENT</div><div class="def-en">a process in which someone forms a plan or idea</div><div class="def-cn">构思，构想，设想</div><div class="relations">→ conceive</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">the original conception of the book</div><div class="example-cn">此书最初的构想</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">3</span><div class="grammar">[countable C, uncountable U]</div><div class="def-en">the process by which a woman or female animal becomes pregnant, or the time when this happens</div><div class="def-cn">受孕；怀孕</div><div class="relations">→ conceive</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">the moment of conception</div><div class="example-cn">受孕的一刻</div></div></div></section>
- CorpusHTML: <section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">conception</div><ul><li>Rheinhold argues that life does not begin at conception.</li><li>In rabbinic canon law, the rabbi explained, human life does not simply begin at conception.</li><li>If we adopt the more expansive conception of democracy which has been used throughout this book, the case is even stronger.</li><li>And, indeed, his theory is firmly rooted in his conception of equilibrium.</li><li>Since its conception, two of the airlines that used the old airport as a hub have disappeared.</li><li>An enactment which threatened the essential elements of any plausible conception of democratic government would lie beyond those boundaries.</li><li>We can take as one starting point Tocqueville&#x27;s conception of democracy, which I have already briefly sketched in the Introduction.</li><li>Straczynski is responsible not only for the conception of the show, but for most of its scripts.</li><li>A constructivist would deny the existence of anything that corresponds to this conception of a phenomenal screen.</li><li>For in fact, Co-operation does not fit comfortably into the Webbs&#x27; conception of Socialism.</li></ul></section><section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">have (no) conception of something</div><ul><li>And in historical terms, many societies have no conception of a distinct political order.</li><li>They have no conception of what women really feel and want!</li><li>You seem to have no conception of where we stand!</li><li>We have no conception of the interconnections that influence us in our associations of words and meanings.</li><li>Until you have known it you will have no conception of what it is to be truly lonely.</li><li>It is true enough to say that we would have no conception of it.</li></ul></section>

- DefinitionsHTML: <section class="pos-block"><div class="pos-title">noun <span class="pron">/kənˈtenʃən/</span></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">1</span><div class="phrase">claim</div><div class="grammar">[countable C]</div><div class="register">formal</div><div class="activator">SAY/STATE</div><div class="def-en">a strong opinion that someone expresses</div><div class="def-cn">论点，主张</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">Her main contention is that doctors should do more to encourage healthy eating.</div><div class="example-cn">她的主要观点是医生应该更多地鼓励健康的饮食习惯。</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">2</span><div class="phrase">at bone</div><div class="grammar">[uncountable U]</div><div class="register">formal</div><div class="activator">ARGUE</div><div class="def-en">argument and disagreement between people</div><div class="def-cn">争论，争端，口角</div><div class="patterns"><span class="label">Pattern</span> source/area/point of contention</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">The issue of hunting is a source of contention.</div><div class="example-cn">狩猎问题是争论的焦点。</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">3</span><div class="phrase">in contention</div><div class="activator">ARGUE</div><div class="def-en">having a chance of winning something</div><div class="def-cn">有获胜机会</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">Owen’s goal kept England in contention.</div><div class="example-cn">欧文的入球使英格兰队有望获胜。</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">4</span><div class="phrase">out of contention</div><div class="def-en">no longer having a chance of winning something</div><div class="def-cn">失去获胜机会</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">Injury has put him out of contention for the title.</div><div class="example-cn">受伤使他失去了夺冠机会。</div></div></div></section>
- CorpusHTML: <section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">kept... in contention</div><ul><li>Three penalties by Hobbs kept Bradford firmly in contention and another soon after the interval levelled the scores at 8-8.</li></ul></section><section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">contention</div><ul><li>But some of his contentions seem overstated.</li><li>A key area of contention is the call for the wilderness to be opened to oil and gas drilling.</li><li>Exactly how many years remains a point of contention.</li><li>Another point of contention is financial.</li><li>The main point of contention now is not whether, but how long a scaled-down force should remain.</li><li>The respondent&#x27;s contention is that there is a difference between a public and a private Act.</li><li>I could see the contention in his wrinkled face.</li><li>The contention continued for four years and the underlying reason for it was pique.</li></ul></section><section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">source/area/point of contention</div><ul><li>This surface interval between leaving the bell and entering the decompression chamber, became a point of contention within the medical profession.</li><li>This is, of course, a point of contention which will not be pursued here but is useful to bear in mind.</li><li>How long he stays a King is a point of contention.</li><li>Another point of contention is financial.</li><li>Trifling though they may appear, these are the conventionally cited points of contention between the Celtic and Roman churches.</li><li>The main point of contention now is not whether, but how long a scaled-down force should remain.</li><li>Public consultation is our second major point of contention.</li></ul></section>
- OriginHTML: <div class="origin">contention (1300-1400) Old French Latin contentio, from contendere; → CONTEND</div>

- DefinitionsHTML: <section class="pos-block"><div class="pos-title">noun <span class="pron">/kənˌtɪnjuˈeɪʃən/</span></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">1</span><div class="grammar">[countable C]</div><div class="activator">CONTINUE/NOT STOP</div><div class="def-en">something that continues or follows something else that has happened before, without a stop or change</div><div class="def-cn">延续，继续部分</div><div class="patterns"><span class="label">Pattern</span> continuation of</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">The present economic policy is a continuation of the earlier one.</div><div class="example-cn">现在的经济政策是以前政策的延续。</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">2</span><div class="grammar">[uncountable U]</div><div class="activator">CONTINUOUS</div><div class="def-en">the continuation of something is the fact that it continues to exist or happen</div><div class="def-cn">继续；连续；持续</div><div class="patterns"><span class="label">Pattern</span> continuation of</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">measures to ensure the continuation of food supplies</div><div class="example-cn">确保食品持续供应的措施</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">3</span><div class="grammar">[countable C]</div><div class="activator">JOIN something TOGETHER</div><div class="def-en">something that joins something else as if it were part of it</div><div class="def-cn">延续物，接续物</div><div class="patterns"><span class="label">Pattern</span> continuation of</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">The Baltic Sea is a continuation of the North Sea.</div><div class="example-cn">波罗的海是北海的延伸。</div></div></div></section>

- DefinitionsHTML: <section class="pos-block"><div class="pos-title">noun <span class="homnum">1</span> <span class="pron">/ˈkɜːtəsi/</span></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">1</span><div class="grammar">[uncountable U]</div><div class="activator">POLITE</div><div class="def-en">polite behaviour and respect for other people</div><div class="def-cn">有礼的举止，礼貌</div><div class="relations">SYN politeness · OPP discourtesy</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">It’s a matter of common courtesy to acknowledge letters.</div><div class="example-cn">确认收到来信是起码的礼貌。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">He didn’t even have the courtesy to call and say he couldn’t come.</div><div class="example-cn">他甚至连打个电话来说一声他不能来的礼貌都没有。</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">2</span><div class="grammar">[countable C]</div><div class="activator">POLITE</div><div class="def-en">something you do or say to be polite</div><div class="def-cn">礼貌的行为 [话]</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">The two men exchanged courtesies before getting down to business.</div><div class="example-cn">两个人互致问候，然后开始谈论正事。</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">3</span><div class="phrase">(by) courtesy of somebody</div><div class="activator">GIVE</div><div class="def-en">by someone’s permission or kindness, rather than by paying them</div><div class="def-cn">承蒙某人的允许；由于某人的好意〔而不是因为付了钱〕</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">photographs supplied courtesy of Blenheim Palace</div><div class="example-cn">承蒙布伦海姆宫提供的照片</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">4</span><div class="phrase">(by) courtesy of something</div><div class="def-en">if one thing happens courtesy of another, the second thing caused the first</div><div class="def-cn">由某事引起，因某事造成</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">Healy received a deep cut on his left hand, courtesy of Nicole’s ice skate.</div><div class="example-cn">希利因为尼科尔的冰鞋左手被划出了一道深深的伤口。</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">5</span><div class="phrase">do somebody the courtesy of doing something</div><div class="def-en">to be polite enough to do something for someone</div><div class="def-cn">为对某人表示礼貌而做某事</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">At least do me the courtesy of telling the truth.</div><div class="example-cn">至少请你告诉我实情。</div></div></div></section><section class="pos-block"><div class="pos-title">adjective <span class="homnum">2</span></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">1</span><div class="def-en">provided free to a customer by a company</div><div class="def-cn">〔由公司〕免费提供的</div><div class="patterns"><span class="label">Pattern</span> courtesy bus/taxi/car/phone etc</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">The hotel runs a courtesy bus from the airport.</div><div class="example-cn">这家酒店在机场有免费巴士接送。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">Most reviewers receive a courtesy copy of the book.</div><div class="example-cn">大多数书评家都收到一本赠书。</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">2</span><div class="phrase">courtesy visit/call</div><div class="def-en">a visit etc done to be polite or show respect</div><div class="def-cn">礼节性拜访</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">Our captain put in a courtesy visit during dinner.</div><div class="example-cn">席间，我们的队长作了礼节性拜访。</div></div></div></section>

Gentleman does not have to worry about the normal courtesy of staying to listen to the next speaker.</li><li>Reproduced courtesy of the Wykeham Galleries Procedure I stand at an easel to paint.</li><li>We enclose a stamped, addressed envelope for the courtesy of your reply.</li><li>I also owed Maggie the courtesy of letting her know I didn&#x27;t need her to do my legwork any longer.</li></ul></section><section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">do somebody the courtesy of doing something</div><ul><li>He always did us the courtesy of a reply, mind.</li></ul></section><section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">courtesy</div><ul><li>As a courtesy to other diners, we ask that all cell phones be left at the door.</li><li>Businessmen value the service and courtesy offered by traditional hotels.</li><li>He had been a model of courtesy.</li><li>I don&#x27;t think she wanted us to come and stay with her, she just offered out of courtesy.</li><li>I wish he&#x27;d had the courtesy to tell me when he was coming back.</li><li>Odds are that the other person will return the courtesy of an introduction.</li><li>When you contact a government office, you should receive efficient service and be treated with courtesy.</li></ul></section><section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">have the courtesy to do something</div><ul><li>The hon. Gentleman should have the courtesy to recognise that a considerable amount is being done.</li></ul></section><section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">exchanged courtesies</div><ul><li>When wandering over the hills we met a shepherd, exchanged courtesies, and offered him a glass.</li></ul></section><section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">courtesy visit/call</div><ul><li>To this end an unofficial courtesy visit was arranged and in August 1857 the Imperial couple came to Osborne.</li></ul></section><section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">courtesy bus/taxi/car/phone etc</div><ul><li>Not all the players get courtesy cars.</li><li>He began the two-mile journey from the hotel in a courtesy car at 9.25 a. m.</li><li>Standing on the courtesy bus I watched their last-minute dash to catch the folding doors with relief.</li><li>A courtesy bus operates between the two several times a day.</li><li>A courtesy bus runs regularly into the centre of Sorrento and local buses stop nearby.</li></ul></section>

class="activator">MAKING SEVERE JUDGMENTS · CRITICIZE</div><div class="def-en">if you are critical, you criticize someone or something</div><div class="def-cn">批评的，批判的</div><div class="patterns"><span it</div><div class="def-cn">紧要的，关键性的</div><div class="patterns"><span class="label">Pattern</span> critical to</div><div class="relations">SYN crucial</div><div class="example"><div critical for us to know the truth.</div><div class="example-cn">我们知道真相是极其重要的。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">Foreign trade is of critical importance to the economy.</div><div class="example-en">The fighting has stopped, but the situation is still critical.</div><div class="example-cn">战斗已经停止，但形势依然严峻。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">changes that took place during the critical period at the end of the war</div><div class="example-cn">战争临近结束的关键时期内所发生的变化</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">4</span><div class="def-en">so ill class="example-cn">她在接受特别护理，病情危急但稳定。</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">5</span><div class="phrase">the critical list</div><div class="patterns"><span class="example-cn">星期日晚上仍有两名受害人病危。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">He was taken off the critical list and is now in a stable condition.</div><div class="example-cn">他已经脱离危险，现在病情稳定。</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">6</span><div class="activator">MAKING FAIR JUDGMENTS · JUDGE</div><div class="def-en">making careful judgments about how good or bad something is</div><div class="def-cn">判断审慎的，评判严谨的</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">His book provides a critical analysis of the television industry in Britain.</div><div class="example-cn">他的书对英国的电视行业作了审慎的分析。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">She looked round the room with a critical eye.</div><div class="example-cn">她以评判的眼光环视房间。</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">7</span><div class="activator">ART/FILM/BOOKS ETC · ART/CULTURE</div><div class="def-en">according to critics said it was very good).</div><div class="example-cn">这本书去年出版，受到高度评价。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">Her first play was a critical success (= critics said it was good).</div><div class="example-cn">她的第一部剧本受到好评。</div></div></div></section>

- DefinitionsHTML: <section class="pos-block"><div class="pos-title">verb <span class="pron">/dɪˈraɪv/</span></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">1</span><div class="grammar">[transitive T]</div><div class="activator">GET</div><div class="def-en">to get something, especially an advantage or a pleasant feeling, from something</div><div class="def-cn">得到，获得〔优势或愉快的感受〕</div><div class="patterns"><span class="label">Pattern</span> derive pleasure/enjoyment etc</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">Medically, we will derive great benefit from this technique.</div><div class="example-cn">从医学的角度来讲，这一技术将使我们受益匪浅。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">Many students derived enormous satisfaction from the course.</div><div class="example-cn">许多学生从这门课程中得到了巨大的满足。</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">2</span><div class="grammar">[intransitive I, transitive T]</div><div class="activator">COME FROM/ORIGINATE</div><div class="def-en">to develop or come from something else</div><div class="def-cn">源自，源于</div><div class="patterns"><span class="label">Pattern</span> derive from</div><div class="relations">→ derivation</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">This word is derived from Latin.</div><div class="example-cn">该词源自拉丁语。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">patterns of behaviour that derive from basic beliefs</div><div class="example-cn">源于基本信仰的行为模式</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">3</span><div class="grammar">[transitive T]</div><div class="register">technical</div><div class="def-en">to get a chemical substance from another substance</div><div class="def-cn">提取〔化学物质〕</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">The enzyme is derived from human blood.</div><div class="example-cn">这种酶是从人体血液中提取的。</div></div></div></section>
- UsageHTML: <section class="usage-box"><div class="usage-title">Register</div><div class="usage-en">In everyday English, people usually say that something comes from something rather than is derived from something:</div><div class="usage-cn">在日常英语中, 人们一般用 come from 表示 “ 源自 ” 的意思, 而不用 be derived from</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">This word comes from Latin.</div><div class="example-cn">该词源自拉丁语。</div></div></section>
- CorpusHTML: <section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">derive</div><ul><li>The process used to derive criteria commenced with a general view of the learning objectives to be focused upon.</li><li>A country can also derive export revenue from service income, e. g. shipping and tourism, together with remittances from overseas workers.</li><li>Which suggests that the life patterns imposed on infants in fact derive from biological need.</li><li>They also denote deliberate obfuscations deriving from Dada and Surrealism.</li><li>This Board rejected both these submissions and held that the profits did not arise in or derive from Hong Kong.</li><li>One of the first commercial products to derive from this biotechnology is likely to be genetically engineered tomatoes.</li><li>Throughout his early adult life he passed from one religious system to another, unable to derive lasting spiritual satisfaction form any.</li><li>Then she decided to wash her hair, thinking she might derive some comfort from this familiar rite.</li></ul></section><section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">derive something from something</div><ul><li>Hughes&#x27; music is derived from blues and jazz.</li><li>Children derive comfort from familiar surroundings.</li><li>The enzyme is derived from human blood.</li><li>Many colleges derive most of their income from tuition fees.</li></ul></section><section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">be derived from something</div><ul><li>This prediction is derived from a free-form textual description of the problem.</li><li>The knowledge is derived from the actual relationships implicit in the data.</li><li>There are several possible ways of administering tests which might be derived from the Cockcroft Committee&#x27;s recommendations.</li><li>Disease activity must therefore be derived from the degree of abnormal bowel uptake on abdominal scans.</li><li>The drink and drug revenue, too, is derived from the poor.</li><li>The following problem solving technique is derived from the practice of work study and management consultancy.</li><li>The cognitive schemata of the adult are derived from the sensorimotor schemata of the child.</li></ul></section>
- OriginHTML: <div class="origin">derive (1300-1400) French dériver, from Latin derivare “ to draw out water ”, from rivus “ stream ”</div>

- DefinitionsHTML: <section class="pos-block"><div class="pos-title">verb <span class="pron">/dɪˈtrækt/</span></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">1</span><div class="phrase">detract from something</div><div class="activator">SPOIL</div><div class="def-en">to make something seem less good</div><div class="def-cn">减低，破坏，损害</div><div class="relations">OPP enhance</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">One mistake is not going to detract from your achievement.</div><div class="example-cn">一个失误无损于你的成就。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">Litter detracts from the appearance of the town.</div></div></div></section>
- CorpusHTML: <section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">detract from</div><ul><li>We need to ask whether the interest in Machiavellian behaviour is detracting from the positive side of political activity.</li><li>This would allow some room for choice, but would not detract from the fundamental notion of a centrally planned service.</li><li>It would also detract from the open aspect of the field and more generally from the landscape character of the areas.</li><li>Some observers worry that the role of landlord will detract from the primary business of five-star hotels.</li><li>Her striking mannerisms detract from the reality of the character.</li><li>They felt that the proposed development would detract from the rural character of the area because of its size, height and bulk.</li><li>All this was strategy he had developed to detract from their discrepancy in height.</li><li>Any fears that either food or service might detract from this otherwise delightful scene were immediately dismissed -- both are excellent.</li></ul></section><section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">detract</div><ul><li>No amount of display or pomp is going to increase it, or lack of it detract.</li><li>I think this is a very convenient sort of way to detract attention from much more serious problems.</li><li>However, these are insufficient to detract from a very readable and extensive account of modern mass spectrometry.</li><li>Some observers worry that the role of landlord will detract from the primary business of five-star hotels.</li><li>Her striking mannerisms detract from the reality of the character.</li><li>The omission of these chapters will not detract from your general appreciation of homoeopathy.</li><li>For instance, if there is one other woman engineer she may detract from your special status.</li></ul></section>
- OriginHTML: <div class="origin">detract (1400-1500) Latin detractus, past participle of detrahere “ to take away ”</div>

- UsageHTML: <section class="usage-box"><div class="usage-title">Register</div><div class="usage-en">In everyday English, people usually say boring rather than dull:</div><div class="usage-cn">在日常英语中, 人们一般说 boring, 而不说 dull</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">a long, boring film</div><div class="example-cn">一部冗长而沉闷的电影</div></div></section>

but dull this morning, with the possibility of showers later in the day.</li><li>His head hit the floor with a dull thud.</li><li>This kind of mindless work can become very dull very backs.</li><li>Sleep away the tiredness and the dull ache inside his head, that was the thing to do.</li><li>It seemed that here, there was never any spring, only wind and rain and the dull ache of loss.</li><li>It starts as a dull ache that gradually evolves into a severe throbbing pain, centering in the frontal and temporal regions.</li><li>It wasn&#x27;t really very bad but it was a dull ache that made her realise she would never get to sleep.</li></ul></section><section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">dull thud</div><ul><li>As he moved along the rows of guns, his wooden leg dull thud behind his left knee.</li><li>The gunshots were no longer dull thuds echoing off the hill but reports, punctuated by the snapping of triggers.</li><li>There were dull thuds from the cargo hold.</li><li>Plastic produces a dull thud, while glass gives a high-pitched clink.</li></ul></section><section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">dull</div><ul><li>But those wines give only momentary pleasure and thereafter the senses are dulled and the mind is clouded.</li><li>As soon as a leaf dries, it begins to dull, lacking the luminescence that one full of juices diet.</div><div class="example-cn">饮食中应该避免摄入高脂肪食物。</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">2</span><div class="activator">BEAT/DEFEAT</div><div class="def-en">to defeat a team or person in a competition, so that they no longer take part in it</div><div class="def-cn">〔在比赛中〕淘汰</div><div class="relations">SYN knock out</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">Our team was eliminated in the first round.</div><div class="example-cn">我们队第一轮就被淘汰了。</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">3</span><div class="phrase">kill</div><div class="activator">KILL</div><div class="def-en">to kill someone in order to prevent them from causing trouble</div><div class="def-cn">消灭，铲除</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">a ruthless dictator who eliminated all his rivals</div><div class="example-cn">铲除所有异己的残酷独裁者</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">4</span><div class="phrase">eliminate somebody from class="def-cn">〔警方〕将某人排除在调查对象之外</div></div></section>
- UsageHTML: <section class="usage-box"><div class="usage-title">Register</div><div class="usage-en">In everyday English, people usually say get rid of rather than eliminate:</div><div class="usage-cn">在日常英语中，人们一般说 get rid of ，而不说 eliminate</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">It is almost impossible to get rid of the problem.</div><div class="example-cn">要摆脱这个问题几乎是不可能的。</div></div></section>
- CorpusHTML: <section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">eliminate</div><ul><li>His scheme involves eliminating 100,000 parking places and installing 15,000 parking-meters.</li><li>The car maker said it will eliminate 74,000 jobs over the next four years.</li><li>The dictator eliminated anyone who might be a threat to him.</li><li>Traffic police intend to eliminate congestion caused by illegally parked vehicles.</li><li>The Colts were eliminated in the first round of the playoffs.</li><li>Having to live with big risks that can not be eliminated makes living with the little risks of life seem natural.</li><li>The parents were able to eliminate the intimidating outbursts almost entirely.</li><li>Advances in medical science have eliminated the need for many patients to spend long periods of time in hospital.</li><li>He supposes that technological process will eliminate the problem of scarcity of resources.</li></ul></section><section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">eliminate a need/possibility/risk/problem etc</div><ul><li>In contrast, the engineer&#x27;s ambition is to control, to organise, to plan and to eliminate risks.</li><li>Research will never eliminate risk, but it minimizes it.</li></ul></section>

- DefinitionsHTML: <section class="pos-block"><div class="pos-title">adjective <span class="pron">/ˈevɪdənt/</span></div><div class="sense"><div class="activator">OBVIOUS</div><div class="def-en">easy to see, notice, or understand</div><div class="def-cn">明显的；明白的</div><div class="patterns"><span class="label">Pattern</span> evident to · evident in</div><div class="relations">SYN obvious ·, clear</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">It was evident that she was unhappy.</div><div class="example-cn">她显然不开心。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">It soon became evident that she was seriously ill.</div><div class="example-cn">大家很快就明白她病得很重。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">It was clearly evident that the company was in financial difficulties.</div><div class="example-cn">很明显，公司陷入了财务困境。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">It was evident to me that he was not telling the truth.</div><div class="example-cn">我十分清楚他没说实话。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">The growing popularity of the subject is evident in the numbers of students wanting to study it.</div><div class="example-cn">这门课程越来越受欢迎，从想修读此课程的学生人数上即可明显看出这一点。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">Bob ate his lunch with evident enjoyment.</div><div class="example-cn">显然鲍勃吃午饭吃得津津有味。</div></div></div></section>
- CorpusHTML: <section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">evident</div><ul><li>Neither Hoffert nor Lembke replied, but their pride was evident.</li><li>Whether we choose to focus on military security or protection of the environment, the policy relevance of our research is evident.</li><li>But even more evident has been the growth of a new class of wealth.</li><li>Carlos&#x27; frustration was evident in his comments.</li><li>It could now become evident that she had a good figure.</li><li>It is evident that the machine aesthetic played more than just a stylistic part in the revolution.</li><li>His belief in divine aid was evident to all.</li></ul></section><section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">evident that</div><ul><li>For some time it has been evident that all I am to you is a vessel to receive your seed.</li><li>As the decade drew to a close, it was evident that consumers were fed up.</li><li>It was evident that Mrs Gracie&#x27;s departure had been noted.</li><li>From our earlier discussion it is evident that opinion is divided amongst those who have tried to evaluate national programmes.</li><li>It is evident that she values his appearance more than his other virtues and still considers his profession a drawback.</li><li>It quickly became evident that the attack was not going according to plan.</li><li>It rapidly became evident that this clinic could not make even a dent in the problem.</li><li>Nowhere was this more evident that within official portraiture.</li></ul></section>
- OriginHTML: <div class="origin">evident (1300-1400) French Latin evidens, from e- “ out ” + the present participle of videre “ to see ”</div>

- DefinitionsHTML: <section class="pos-block"><div class="pos-title">noun <span class="pron">/ɪkˈsepʃən/</span></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">1</span><div class="activator">EXCEPT</div><div class="def-en">something or someone that is not included in a general statement or does not follow a rule or pattern</div><div class="def-cn">例外，除外</div><div class="patterns"><span class="label">Pattern</span> notable/important/significant exception · minor/major exception</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">It’s been cold, but today’s an exception.</div><div class="example-cn">天气一直寒冷，但今天是个例外。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">We all laughed, with the exception of Maggie.</div><div class="example-cn">除了玛吉，我们都笑了。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">Each plant, without exception, contains some kind of salt.</div><div class="example-cn">每一种植物都含有某种盐分，无一例外。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">With one or two notable exceptions, there are few women conductors.</div><div class="example-cn">很少有女性指挥，除了一两位是明显的例外。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">With a few minor exceptions, the new edition is much like the previous one.</div><div class="example-cn">除了有几处细小的改动之外，新版本与前一版没有什么两样。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">The law applies to all EU countries; I’m afraid Rhea’s the exception that proves the rule.</div><div class="example-cn">这里的大多数人都很敬业，恐怕雷亚是其中的例外。</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">3</span><div class="phrase">take exception to something</div><div class="activator">OFFEND</div><div class="def-en">to be angry or upset because of something</div><div class="def-cn">因某事而生气 [烦恼]</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">Tom took great exception to my remark about Americans.</div><div class="example-cn">汤姆对我有关美国人的评论极为不满。</div></div></div></section>
- CorpusHTML: <section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">somebody/something is the exception that proves the rule</div><ul><li>Most people our age have finished school, and Mike is the exception that proves the rule.</li></ul></section><section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">take exception to something</div><ul><li>Not that, for the most part, there was much that visitors could take exception to.</li><li>What I take exception to is the manner in which we are presently carrying out our naval preparations.</li><li>Jones took exception to a comment I made about his weight.</li><li>They had not taken exception to it before, so why start now?</li><li>Paul took exception to her advice and resigned.</li><li>Louise picked out a pretty little pink dress that nobody could possibly take exception to and so honour was satisfied.</li><li>No one could possibly take exception to this Mathis infant.</li><li>Dunbar could scarcely take exception to that, and changed the subject.</li><li>Owen thought for a moment that he was taking exception to the casual obscenity, but it was not that.</li></ul></section><section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">exception</div><ul><li>A curious fact which might seem at first to constitute an exception to this explanation turns out to provide further confirmation of it.</li><li>There is, however, an exception.</li><li>Most couples who break up seem to find it hard to remain friends. Kim and Gerry are exceptions to that rule.</li><li>There are exceptions, of course.</li><li>The big exception is the most vital crop of all: sugar.</li><li>I had no choice but to cut back to a hands-off style-getting involved in exceptions only.</li><li>There are many exceptions, though: In some but not most traditional human societies, men move to women.</li><li>With a few minor exceptions, the legal system in the two countries is very similar.</li><li>Women do not usually get to the top in politics, but there have been a few notable exceptions.</li><li>With rare exceptions, world champions are bullied and beaten into fighting shape on the streets.</li><li>Most of the students did well, though there were one or two exceptions.</li><li>After discussion it was agreed that the Committee be re-elected as it was, with two exceptions.</li></ul></section><section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">with the exception of somebody/something</div><ul><li>Ragworm is the principal flounder bait with the exception of May and June when peeler crab will produce.</li><li>There was a full turn up of Liberal ministers, with the exception of Lloyd George.</li><li>Everyone was more interested in playing than reading - with the exception of Steve Vai, that is.</li><li>They represent the set of minimal units required to uniquely specify a word, with the exception of homophones.</li></ul></section>

- UsageHTML: <section class="usage-box"><div class="usage-title">Register</div><div class="usage-en">In everyday English, people usually say leave something or someone out rather than exclude something or someone:</div><div class="usage-cn">在日常英语中，人们一般说 leave something/someone out ，而不说 exclude something/someone</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">Some information was left out of the report.</div><div class="example-cn">有些消息报道中并没有提到。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">We didn’t mean to leave you out.</div><div class="example-cn">我们并非故意把你遗漏的。</div></div></section>

class="sense-no">8</span><div class="phrase">shake/rock the foundations of something</div><div class="activator">CHANGE/BECOME DIFFERENT</div><div class="def-en">to completely change the way something class="example-cn">大家接到约定信号后都必须静止不动的一个游戏</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">3</span><div class="phrase">be given to (doing) something</div><div class="def-cn">往往会做某事〔尤指不该做的事〕</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">He was a quiet man, not usually given to complaining.</div><div class="def-en">to accept that something is true or exists, especially when you are developing an idea or argument</div><div class="def-cn">认为某事理所当然如此，认为某事是想当然〔尤用于得出观点〕</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">The fact that people find change difficult is taken as given.</div><div class="example-cn">人总觉得改变什么很难，这是毫无疑问的。</div></div></div></section><section class="pos-block"><div class="example-en">Sandra will be at least 15 minutes late – that’s a given.</div><div class="example-cn">桑德拉至少会迟到 15 分钟，这是肯定的。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">The concept is reinterpretation of Liberal principles.</li><li>Not all of either circumstance was required for the effect, given that the other whole circumstance existed.</li></ul></section><section nature are regarded as inexorable givens.</li><li>They were, like this new body she was growing into, givens.</li><li>We might say roughly that there are two sorts of givens which we could call duties and wishes.</li><li>It enters into the work as one of the givens with which the artist begins.</li><li>National identities are not constant and unchanging givens.</li></ul></section><section structure of your project needs to be visible, almost at a glance.</li><li>That Holy Trinity is different from most Catholic parishes is evident at a glance.</li><li>Garden rooms A small garden that of police.</li><li>Here are the weekend football scores at a glance.</li><li>You can see at a glance the few places other readers lingered Over.</li><li>I could see at a glance that the situation was class="corpus-title">at first glance/sight</div><ul><li>At first glance this will probably sound strange, yet there is a way in which it is also logical.</li><li>At first glance, it looked like unalloyed good news.</li><li>At first glance, the place seemed deserted.</li></ul></section><section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">glance</div><ul><li>At a glance you know what&#x27;s touch, strong feelings that show.</li><li>A glance at my watch showed that it was nearly five and I was bored to death.</li><li>I walked away without a wave or a backward glance.</li><li>They&#x27;d exchanged one brief glance only since she&#x27;d run from the stable that morning.</li><li>At first glance, Cowley thought, he looked like a retired accountant.</li><li>She did not let her glance fall sideboard.</li><li>She gave one glance towards Rose, then looked away.</li><li>He, too, gave Robert a glance.</li></ul></section>

- DefinitionsHTML: <section class="pos-block"><div class="pos-title">noun <span class="pron">/heɪst/</span></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">1</span><div class="activator">HURRY</div><div class="def-en">great speed in doing something, especially because you do not have enough time</div><div class="def-cn">匆忙，仓促</div><div class="relations">SYN hurry</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">I soon regretted my haste.</div><div class="example-cn">我很快就对自己的仓促感到后悔。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">In his haste to leave, he forgot his briefcase.</div><div class="example-cn">他走得很匆忙，忘了带公文包。</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">2</span><div class="phrase">in haste</div><div class="register">written · formal</div><div class="activator">HURRY</div><div class="def-en">quickly or in a hurry</div><div class="def-cn">匆忙地，急忙地</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">They left in haste, without even saying goodbye.</div><div class="example-cn">他们走得很匆忙，连再见都没说。</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">3</span><div class="phrase">make haste</div><div class="register">old use</div><div class="activator">HURRY</div><div class="def-en">to hurry or do something quickly</div><div class="def-cn">赶紧，连忙</div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">4</span><div class="phrase">more haste less speed</div><div class="activator">HURRY</div><div class="def-en">used to say that it is better to do something slowly, because if you do it too quickly you will make mistakes</div><div class="def-cn">欲速则不达</div></div></section>
- UsageHTML: <section class="usage-box"><div class="usage-title">Register</div><div class="usage-en">In everyday English, people usually say hurry rather than haste:</div><div class="usage-cn">在日常英语中，人们一般说 hurry ，而不说 haste</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">In my hurry, I left my coat behind.</div><div class="example-cn">我匆匆忙忙的，忘了拿外套。</div></div></section>
- CorpusHTML: <section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">in haste</div><ul><li>In his haste to leave, he almost forgot his coat.</li><li>She had married in haste and regretted it ever since.</li><li>The army retreated in haste.</li></ul></section><section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">make haste</div><ul><li>When he saw Edwin Chase striding up towards them he made haste to make known one to the other.</li><li>Roosevelt towards the end of his life seemed content to make haste slowly.</li><li>We made haste inside, horse, carriage, and all.</li></ul></section><section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">haste</div><ul><li>She scaled its steep side in breathless haste.</li><li>Here haste not only wastes, it kills.</li><li>They were on the run, and in haste, or we should all be dead men.</li><li>I had to write in haste.</li><li>More haste, less speed, Madam!</li><li>Complex negotiations followed, in an atmosphere of haste, as Reagan would take office on January 20.</li><li>There was a trickle of traffic, now, and she overtook the sleepy drivers with an almost reckless haste.</li><li>But who comes in such haste in riding-robes?</li></ul></section><section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">in your haste to do something</div><ul><li>Callinicos, in his haste to counter aestheticism, reduces the aesthetic.</li><li>Maybe I was blotting out my past, as provincials do, in my haste to get to where the action was.</li><li>Then she rushed back towards the stairs, almost falling in her haste to get back to the ground floor.</li><li>He shrugged out of his jacket and her hands went to his cotton shirt, fumbling in their haste to undo the buttons.</li><li>The vultures eat greedily, fighting over scraps, slipping off the rock in their haste to consume.</li></ul></section>
- OriginHTML: <div class="origin">haste (1200-1300) Old French</div>

- CorpusHTML: <section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">imitate</div><ul><li>I had the ability to imitate.</li><li>Our methods have been imitated all over the world.</li><li>He has a unique ability to imitate any sound he has heard.</li><li>And a clear case of life imitating astrology.</li><li>&quot;Don&#x27;t you talk to me like that!&quot; she said imitating her mother&#x27;s high-pitched voice.</li><li>They respond in sympathy to what she is doing and imitate her movements.</li><li>An animal acquires the behaviour pattern by imitating it from another.</li><li>A lot of writers have tried to imitate Lawrence&#x27;s style.</li><li>She&#x27;s really good at imitating our teacher&#x27;s Scottish accent.</li><li>It was as if the ecology of the place had chosen to imitate politics.</li><li>We imitated the styles of Conrad, Hemingway, and Time magazine.</li><li>They still resent the deep disappointment that has followed attempts to imitate the West.</li></ul></section>

- DefinitionsHTML: <section class="pos-block"><div class="pos-title">adjective <span class="pron">/ɪmˈplɪsɪt/</span></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">1</span><div class="activator">SUGGEST</div><div class="def-en">suggested or understood without being stated directly</div><div class="def-cn">含蓄的，未言明的</div><div class="patterns"><span class="label">Pattern</span> implicit criticism/threat/assumption</div><div class="relations">OPP explicit</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">Her words contained an implicit threat.</div><div class="example-cn">她话里暗含威胁。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">His statement is being seen as implicit criticism of the work of research laboratories.</div><div class="example-cn">部长的话被认为是对研究实验室工作的含蓄批评。</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">2</span><div class="register">formal</div><div class="activator">THINK SO/NOT BE SURE</div><div class="def-en">forming a central part of something, but without being openly stated</div><div class="def-cn">隐含其中的；内含的</div><div class="patterns"><span class="label">Pattern</span> implicit in</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">Confidentiality is implicit in your relationship with a counselor.</div><div class="example-cn">在你与顾问的关系中，保守秘密是不言而喻的。</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">3</span><div class="activator">COMPLETE</div><div class="def-en">complete and containing no doubts</div><div class="def-cn">完全的，毫无疑问的</div><div class="patterns"><span class="label">Pattern</span> implicit faith/trust/belief</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">They had implicit faith in his powers.</div><div class="example-cn">他们绝对相信他的能力。</div></div></div></section>
- CorpusHTML: <section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">implicit</div><ul><li>Levy&#x27;s statement could be understood as an implicit admission of guilt.</li><li>The very notion of development and change over time is contained within the notion of implicit and explicit aspects of attitudes.</li><li>The clause was criticized by some as giving implicit authority to the army to stage further coups should they be deemed necessary.</li><li>In the case of the land-user, implicit discount rates tend to be very high, particularly for the disadvantaged.</li><li>Planning and reviewing should be implicit in any team meeting - as much as the actual activity.</li><li>Sometimes these are clearly stated but more often than not they are implicit in attitudes and actions.</li><li>Her implicit plan of action is to manage peo-ple in the same fashion she always has.</li><li>It has to be possible to produce spontaneously original sentences which are based on implicit rules which allow generalisation.</li><li>The individual receives an implicit yield on money because of its convenience value as a means of payment.</li></ul></section><section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">implicit criticism/threat/assumption</div><ul><li>In answer, one might presume that implicit justifications can exist to deal with implicit criticisms.</li><li>The second aspect seems even more important: it warns against false generalisations and implicit assumptions.</li><li>It relates to two powerful but implicit assumptions in the messages of women&#x27;s magazines.</li><li>The implicit assumption is that investors can borrow and lend at the riskless rate of interest.</li><li>The implicit threat of disease curtailed summer pleasures for the children of the polio years.</li><li>Is there not an implicit threat of legal proceedings in even the first demand for payment of a debt?</li><li>We begin interactions with an implicit assumption that other people determine and control their behaviour.</li><li>A wartime usefulness was found and implicit criticisms were not developed.</li></ul></section><section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">implicit in</div><ul><li>Implicit in the article is the message that single mothers are responsible for poverty.</li></ul></section><section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">implicit faith/trust/belief</div><ul><li>Hayman had implicit trust in his hit-men, especially against some one he regarded as an old, rusty, washed-up veteran.</li><li>Today few fund managers have such implicit faith in property as an inflation-proof investment.</li><li>The important thing to remember is to have implicit faith in the instrument indications, ignoring any contrary physical sensations.</li></ul></section>

- DefinitionsHTML: <section class="pos-block"><div class="pos-title">adverb <span class="pron">/ɪmˈpɔːtəntli/</span></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">1</span><div class="grammar">[sentence adverb adv]</div><div class="activator">IMPORTANT</div><div class="def-en">used to show that your next statement or question is more, equally etc important than what you said before</div><div class="def-cn">重要的是</div><div class="patterns"><span class="label">Pattern</span> more/most/less/equally importantly</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">Most importantly, you must keep a record of everything you do.</div><div class="example-cn">最重要的是，你必须把你所做的事一一记录下来。</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">2</span><div class="activator">IMPORTANT</div><div class="def-en">in a way that shows you think that what someone is saying or doing is important</div><div class="def-cn">煞有介事地；自以为了不起地</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">He strode importantly into the room.</div><div class="example-cn">他煞有介事地阔步走进房间。</div></div></div></section>
- CorpusHTML: <section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">importantly</div><ul><li>These were accompanied, more importantly, by social policies aimed at encouraging early retirement.</li><li>She walked importantly into the boss&#x27;s office.</li><li>Even more importantly, it supplied many mid-Victorian feminists with a critical perspective on existing social relations.</li><li>More importantly, it was regarded as a distraction from the real issues of environment and development.</li><li>We had a fraud-free election, and most importantly, record turnouts.</li><li>Much more importantly, the Dodgers were always a rock of decency and consistency in a sea of disgusting behavior.</li><li>But more importantly, the network compromised itself repeatedly.</li><li>It is also, most importantly, user-friendly.</li></ul></section><section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">more/most/less/equally importantly</div><ul><li>However, aldosterone is also regulated by sodium and potassium levels and more importantly by the renin-angiotensin system.</li><li>The station was only five minutes away; more importantly, food was only five minutes away.</li><li>Even more importantly, I completely lacked business experience in certain vital parts of the world.</li><li>I received good knowledgeable advice, that worked. and most importantly, I was treated like a human being.</li><li>If food is kept for too long its taste will deteriorate and, more importantly, it may become harmful.</li><li>Perhaps most importantly, the computer interface greatly facilitates both obtaining and recording a complete medical history.</li><li>But more importantly, they can make or break political careers.</li><li>On Bourdieu&#x27;s account these producers are most importantly understood through their habitus, and through their individual strategies and collective struggles.</li></ul></section>

- DefinitionsHTML: <section class="pos-block"><div class="pos-title">adjective <span class="pron">/ɪˈnevətəbəl/</span></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">1</span><div class="phrase">certain</div><div class="activator">CERTAINLY/DEFINITELY</div><div class="def-en">certain to happen and impossible to avoid</div><div class="def-cn">必然发生的，不可避免的</div><div class="patterns"><span class="label">Pattern</span> inevitable consequence/result</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">A further escalation of the crisis now seems inevitable.</div><div class="example-cn">危机的进一步升级现在看来已不可避免。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">It’s inevitable that doctors will make the occasional mistake.</div><div class="example-cn">医生偶尔犯错是难免的。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">Disease was an inevitable consequence of poor living conditions.</div><div class="example-cn">恶劣的生活条件必然诱发疾病。</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">2</span><div class="phrase">the inevitable</div><div class="activator">CERTAINLY/DEFINITELY</div><div class="def-en">a situation that is certain to happen</div><div class="def-cn">不可避免的事情</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">One day the inevitable happened and I got a speeding ticket.</div><div class="example-cn">有一天，不可避免的事情发生了: 我收到了一张超速罚款单。</div></div></div></section>
- CorpusHTML: <section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">the inevitable</div><ul><li>It&#x27;s time they accepted the inevitable and got a divorce.</li><li>Week after week the papers were full of revelations about the minister&#x27;s alleged corrupt dealings, until eventually he bowed to the inevitable and resigned.</li><li>Dinner started with the inevitable chicken soup.</li><li>In the subway I got cornered by the inevitable drunkard wanting to give me some advice.</li><li>One day the inevitable happened and I got a speeding ticket.</li><li>It was a typical student&#x27;s room with the inevitable Van Gogh print on the wall.</li></ul></section><section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">inevitable</div><ul><li>Since the leaders can&#x27;t agree, more fighting is inevitable.</li><li>War now seems inevitable.</li><li>Nina could never escape the inevitable comparisons that people made between her and her twin.</li><li>If the population continues to expand, Ehrlich argues, mass starvation and ecological disaster will be the inevitable consequence.</li><li>Payton handled the inevitable questions about his past with great dignity.</li><li>The price of bread was doubled, with the inevitable result - riots in the streets of Paris.</li><li>It was inevitable that he&#x27;d find out her secret sooner or later.</li></ul></section><section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">it is inevitable (that)</div><ul><li>Winter may seem like a long way off, but it is inevitable.</li><li>The comparison was then premature, but it is inevitable now.</li><li>If any nation decides to plant settlements upon the land of another, it is inevitable that a violent response will follow.</li><li>Perhaps it is inevitable that the relationship should be difficult.</li><li>During this period of transition it is inevitable that we will be teaching the old with the new.</li><li>As an entrepreneur, it is inevitable that you will be buffeted from side to side as you experience the roller coaster.</li><li>From time to time it is inevitable there will be some unwelcome arrivals in the net.</li><li>Speculating about their answers is pointless yet it is inevitable when Mr Garel-Jones&#x27;s resignation letter crosses the boundary of credulity.</li></ul></section>
- OriginHTML: <div class="origin">inevitable (1400-1500) Latin inevitabilis, from evitare “ to avoid ”</div>

- DefinitionsHTML: <section class="pos-block"><div class="pos-title">adjective <span class="pron">/ɪˈreləvənt/</span></div><div class="sense"><div class="activator">CONNECTED WITH</div><div class="def-en">not useful or not relating to a particular situation, and therefore not important</div><div class="def-cn">无关紧要的，不相干的</div><div class="patterns"><span class="label">Pattern</span> largely/totally/completely etc irrelevant · irrelevant to</div><div class="relations">OPP relevant</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">We’re focussing too much on irrelevant details.</div><div class="example-cn">我们过于关注不相干的细节。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">Students viewed Latin as boring and irrelevant.</div><div class="example-cn">学生认为拉丁语无聊且无关紧要。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">His age is completely irrelevant if he can do the job.</div><div class="example-cn">如果他能胜任这份工作，年龄完全不重要。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">The defendant’s lawyer argued that his past offenses were irrelevant to this case.</div><div class="example-cn">被告律师辩称他的前科和本案无关。</div></div></div></section>

- DefinitionsHTML: <section class="pos-block"><div class="pos-title">verb <span class="pron">/ˈaɪsəleɪt/</span></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">1</span><div class="def-en">to separate one person, group, or thing from other people or things</div><div class="def-cn">孤立，隔离</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">The town was isolated by the floods.</div><div class="example-cn">洪水使该镇与外界隔绝。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">The US has sought to isolate Cuba both economically and politically.</div><div class="example-cn">美国一直想在经济和政治上孤立古巴。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">Presley’s phenomenal early success isolated him from his friends.</div><div class="example-cn">普雷斯利年纪轻轻就成就非凡，这使他在朋友中陷于孤立。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">Newborn babies must be isolated from possible contamination.</div><div class="example-cn">新生儿必须隔离，以免受感染。</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">2</span><div class="activator">SEPARATE</div><div class="def-en">if you isolate an idea, problem etc, you consider it separately from other things that are connected with it</div><div class="def-cn">分隔，区别看待〔观点、问题等〕</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">It is impossible to isolate political responsibility from moral responsibility.</div><div class="example-cn">不可能把政治责任和道德责任分离开来。</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">3</span><div class="register">technical</div><div class="activator">SEPARATE</div><div class="def-en">to separate a substance, disease etc from other substances so that it can be studied</div><div class="def-cn">分离〔物质、疾病等以进行研究〕</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">The hepatitis B virus has been isolated from breast milk.</div><div class="example-cn">乙型肝炎病毒已从母乳中分离出来。</div></div></div></section>
- CorpusHTML: <section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">isolate</div><ul><li>Yet it is often a hidden disability, which isolates both the people who suffer from it and their families.</li><li>The U.S. has tried to isolate Cuba both economically and politically.</li><li>The six other patients were immediately isolated from the infected four.</li><li>We used to routinely isolate people who had measles.</li><li>We&#x27;ve succeeded in isolating the gene that determines a person&#x27;s weight.</li><li>Their goal is to surround and isolate the town.</li><li>They may reject you and isolate you because you are different from them and they would like to be like you.</li></ul></section><section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">isolate somebody from somebody</div><ul><li>Presley&#x27;s early success isolated him from his friends.</li><li>Tuberculosis patients are isolated from the other patients.</li></ul></section><section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">isolate something from something</div><ul><li>It is impossible to isolate political responsibility from moral responsibility.</li></ul></section>

- DefinitionsHTML: <section class="pos-block"><div class="pos-title">noun <span class="pron">/ˈlaɪftaɪm/</span></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">1</span><div class="activator">LIFE</div><div class="def-en">the period of time during which someone is alive or something exists</div><div class="def-cn">一生，终生；生存期</div><div class="relations">→ lifespan</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">During her lifetime she had witnessed two world wars.</div><div class="example-cn">她一生亲历了两次世界大战。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">It’s the sort of opportunity you see only once in a lifetime.</div><div class="example-cn">这种机会你一辈子也只能碰到一次。</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">2</span><div class="phrase">the chance/experience etc of a lifetime</div><div class="activator">BEST</div><div class="def-en">the best opportunity, experience etc that you will ever have</div><div class="def-cn">千载难逢 [终生难得] 的机会 / 经历等</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">It was the holiday of a lifetime.</div><div class="example-cn">这样的假期终生难得。</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">3</span><div class="phrase">not in this lifetime</div><div class="register">spoken</div><div class="def-en">not at all</div><div class="def-cn">这辈子是不会了</div><div class="relations">SYN never</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">‘Would you go out with him after he dropped you?’ ‘Not in this lifetime.’</div><div class="example-cn">“ 他甩了你之后你还会和他约会吗？ ” “ 这辈子是不会了。</div></div></div></section>
- CorpusHTML: <section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">the chance/experience etc of a lifetime</div><ul><li>There is also the chance of a lifetime for the talented teams who win through to the final.</li><li>We are offering the experience of a lifetime, and it seems to appeal to people from all over the world.</li><li>Jim assured him that hearing me sing was the experience of a lifetime, but Dad wasn&#x27;t having that.</li><li>This was the chance of a lifetime.</li></ul></section><section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">lifetime</div><ul><li>Would it continue to fascinate for a lifetime?</li><li>The National Medal of Arts award is meant to honor a lifetime of achievement.</li><li>Grief following any death can last a lifetime.</li><li>A good tool should last a lifetime.</li><li>The government had argued that the original military recruiters didn&#x27;t have the authority to offer lifetime health care.</li><li>In our lifetime, ordinary people will travel to the moon.</li><li>All of Callinicos&#x27; philosophical sophistication and matchless political experience evaporate in the face of the art of his own lifetime.</li><li>During Dickinson&#x27;s lifetime, only a few of her works were actually published.</li><li>He suffered a lot of pain in his short lifetime.</li><li>Few women have been so worshipped and detested in their lifetime and by posterity.</li><li>Create something that you love in your lifetime.</li><li>Good looks can last your lifetime!</li></ul></section><section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">once in a lifetime</div><ul><li>The Olympics is a once in a lifetime opportunity.</li><li>Such opportunities are once in a lifetime.</li><li>A beautiful, once in a lifetime waltz, choreographed by the rock.</li><li>This kind of thing happens once in a lifetime.</li><li>The forked road which every star, perhaps every person, faces at least once in a lifetime lay dead ahead.</li><li>The rules are most useful on formal occasions like weddings, and particularly when they happen only once in a lifetime.</li></ul></section>

- DefinitionsHTML: <section class="pos-block"><div class="pos-title">adjective <span class="pron">/ˈluːsɪd/</span></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">1</span><div class="activator">CLEAR/EASY TO UNDERSTAND</div><div class="def-en">expressed in a way that is clear and easy to understand</div><div class="def-cn">表达清楚的，易于理解的</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">You must write in a clear and lucid style.</div><div class="example-cn">你的写作风格一定要清楚易懂。</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">2</span><div class="activator">INTELLIGENT</div><div class="def-en">able to understand and think clearly, used especially about someone who is not always able to do this</div><div class="def-cn">〔尤指总是迷迷糊糊的人〕神志清醒的，头脑清晰的</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">In her more lucid moments the old lady would talk about her past.</div><div class="example-cn">在头脑较清醒的时候，老太太会谈起往事。</div></div></div></section>
- CorpusHTML: <section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">lucid</div><ul><li>Reach out: what is not included in this lucid air?</li><li>a lucid analysis of the situation</li><li>At the moment, Peter is lucid and quite talkative, but his condition is becoming worse.</li><li>Miranda Seymour&#x27;s lucid biography arrives as the general reader&#x27;s guide to Mary Shelley&#x27;s ascent to academic cult status.</li><li>Though small and frail, he was a powerful and lucid debater.</li><li>Churchland&#x27;s Matter and Consciousness is an equally lucid introduction to the philosophy of mind.</li><li>If the doctor thinks the patient isn&#x27;t sufficiently lucid or mature, then the decision should be ignored.</li><li>After finishing, she became lucid, recognized Jung, and greeted him.</li><li>You have such a lucid style.</li></ul></section>
