- CorpusHTML: <section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">massive</div><ul><li>Her house is massive.</li><li>The system is capable of recording massive amounts of information.</li><li>From inside they hear a massive and hysterical scream of the friends letting out their true feelings.</li><li>I had a massive argument with Vicky yesterday.</li><li>Gradually the new global masterplan is falling into place: a series of massive bilateral trade agreements are being struck.</li><li>There is a massive file cabinet stuffed with documents so old and densely packed they may be ready to ignite spontaneously.</li><li>There is massive investment in disease and mortality which the system protects by distracting people&#x27;s attention from it.</li><li>Union leaders are warning of massive job losses.</li><li>The sums involved are massive -- over £12 billion in the first year alone.</li><li>The most influential critics were either misanthropic or committed to the need for massive reform.</li><li>Oswald lay still, aware of a drone in the block, a heaving breath, grimness, massive sleep.</li><li>The ancient temple&#x27;s massive stone pillars had begun to crumble.</li><li>His quarter-measures have brought higher prices, and also provoked massive strikes, but without any prospect of stabilising the economy.</li><li>a massive tax bill</li><li>But de Lattre, personally taking charge, flew in reinforcements and mustered every available aircraft to bomb the massive Vietminh formations.</li></ul></section><section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">massive argument/row etc</div><ul><li>At the time we didn&#x27;t have massive arguments about it.</li><li>The potential for a massive row like that over the community charge was immense.</li></ul></section>

- DefinitionsHTML: <section class="pos-block"><div class="pos-title">adjective <span class="pron">/ˈmɔːbɪd/</span></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">1</span><div class="activator">UNPLEASANT</div><div class="def-en">with a strong and unhealthy interest in unpleasant subjects, especially death</div><div class="def-cn">〔兴趣〕病态的，不健康的；〔尤指〕对死亡着迷的</div><div class="patterns"><span class="label">Pattern</span> morbid fascination/curiosity</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">a morbid fascination with instruments of torture</div><div class="example-cn">对刑具的一种病态的迷恋</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">The trip was made all the worse by Frankie’s morbid fear of flying.</div><div class="example-cn">弗朗基对坐飞机有种病态的恐惧，使得旅途变得更加糟糕。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">His head was full of morbid thoughts.</div><div class="example-cn">他的脑袋里全是不健康的思想。</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">2</span><div class="register">medical</div><div class="def-en">relating to or caused by a disease</div><div class="def-cn">疾病的；疾病引起的</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">a morbid gene</div><div class="example-cn">致病基因</div></div></div></section>
- CorpusHTML: <section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">morbid</div><ul><li>That had always struck me as pretty morbid, but this was the season of goodwill to all men.</li><li>A father&#x27;s self-confidence and certainty were transformed into disorientation, self-doubt and a morbid contemplation of death.</li><li>Le Fanu was not alone in experiencing a morbid convergence between his life and his imaginings.</li><li>But the film has a morbid elegance and an exotic lust for the jugular.</li><li>I didn&#x27;t mind; it kept my thoughts off morbid fancies about Granny in her wooden box.</li><li>Judging from the book&#x27;s sales, people have a morbid fascination with murder.</li><li>a morbid gene</li><li>He walked quickly, his head full of morbid thoughts.</li><li>Some people react so strongly against the morbid view of doubt that they treat doubt casually, even celebrate it.</li><li>You&#x27;re really morbid, you are.</li></ul></section><section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">morbid fascination/curiosity</div><ul><li>Cairns and co focus on the oddities of human nature with a certain morbid curiosity.</li><li>Ken particularly used to enjoy the murder trials - not for any morbid curiosity, but for the drama unfolding.</li><li>Is it morbid fascination that holds your attention?</li></ul></section>
- OriginHTML: <div class="origin">morbid (1600-1700) Latin morbidus “ diseased ”, from morbus “ illness ”</div>

- DefinitionsHTML: <section class="pos-block"><div class="pos-title">adverb <span class="pron">/mɔːrˈəʊvə/</span> <span class="register">formal</span></div><div class="sense"><div class="activator">AND/ALSO</div><div class="def-en">in addition – used to introduce information that adds to or supports what has previously been said</div><div class="def-cn">此外，而且，加之，再者</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">The rent is reasonable and, moreover, the location is perfect.</div><div class="example-cn">租金合理，而且位置也非常好。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">The source of the information is irrelevant. Moreover, the information need not be confidential.</div><div class="example-cn">信息来源无关紧要，而且也不一定必须是机密的。</div></div></div></section>
- UsageHTML: <section class="usage-box"><div class="usage-title">Register</div><div class="usage-en">Moreover is very formal. In everyday English, people use what’s more or also instead:</div><div class="usage-cn">moreover 非常正式。日常英语中用 what’s more 或 also</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">The rent is reasonable and, what’s more, the location is perfect.</div><div class="example-cn">租金合理，而且位置绝佳。</div></div></section>
- CorpusHTML: <section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">moreover</div><ul><li>He should, moreover, be a moderate liberal since that party controlled a majority of the seats in Congress.</li><li>The conditions upon which States receive the funds, moreover, could not be more clearly stated by Congress.</li><li>Coventry, moreover, differed fundamentally from the Stour Valley.</li><li>They were portrayed as more potent and, moreover, incurable.</li><li>Everything suggests, moreover, that Sereny has a special and patient charisma.</li><li>It seems likely, moreover, that the police deliberately avoided mixing it in the more perilous districts.</li><li>Early in the seventeenth century, moreover, the post of premier commis had begun to emerge.</li><li>I had no desire to return, and moreover, the watchman would not let me in anyway.</li><li>Using language is a very complex enterprise. Moreover, there is more to communication than merely putting sentences together.</li></ul></section>

class="example-en">Family photos occupied almost the entire wall.</div><div class="example-cn">家人的照片差不多占了整个墙面。</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">4</span><div class="activator">ENTER</div><div class="def-en">to enter a place in a large group and keep control of it, especially by military force</div><div class="def-cn">〔尤被军队〕占领，占据</div><div class="relations">→ invade</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">an occupying army</div><div class="example-cn">占领军</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">Students occupied Sofia University on Monday.</div><div class="example-cn">星期一学生们占领了索非亚大学。</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">5</span><div class="phrase">occupy somebody’s mind/thoughts/attention</div><div class="activator">THINK ABOUT</div><div class="def-en">if something occupies your mind etc, you think about that thing more than anything else</div><div class="def-cn">占据某人的脑海 / 思想 / 注意力</div><div class="relations">→ preoccupy</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">Work will occupy your mind and help you forget about him.</div><div class="example-cn">工作会占据你的思想，使你忘记他。</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">6</span><div class="def-en">to use something such as a room, seat, or bed</div><div class="def-cn">使用，占用〔房间、座位、床等〕</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">Many patients who are occupying hospital beds could be transferred to other places.</div><div class="example-cn">许多占用医院床位的病人都可以转往其他地方。</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">7</span><div class="def-en">to have an official position or job</div><div class="def-cn">担任〔正式职位或工作〕</div><div class="relations">SYN hold</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">Before becoming prime minister, he had already occupied several cabinet - UsageHTML: <section class="usage-box"><div class="usage-title">Register</div><div class="usage-en">In everyday English, people usually say that something takes up time or space rather than occupies it:</div><div class="usage-cn">在日常英语中，表示某事物占用时间或空间时，人们一般说 take up ，而不说 occupy</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">Work takes up most of her time.</div><div class="example-cn">工作占去了她的大部分时间。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">That bed takes up almost the whole room.</div><div class="example-cn">那张床几乎占据了整个房间。</div></div></section>
- CorpusHTML: <section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">occupy somebody’s mind/thoughts/attention</div><ul><li>While she waited, she tried to occupy her mind with pleasant thoughts of the vacation.</li></ul></section><section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">occupy</div><ul><li>The loss of activity Work will have usually occupied a considerable part of an individual&#x27;s life prior to retirement.</li><li>The cafe occupies a single dimly lit room.</li><li>Debates within the social sciences have occupied an intellectual space which has drawn upon both scientific models and the humanities.</li><li>Fishing occupies most of my spare time.</li><li>He, Kramer, occupied some uncertain position in the middle.</li><li>Agonists are substances which are so similar to a specific neurotransmitter they can occupy that neurotransmitter&#x27;s receptor perfectly.</li><li>Movie stars occupy the large suites on the third floor.</li></ul></section><section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">occupy somebody with (doing) something</div><ul><li>One-plant cultures of a single species developed vegetatively, occupying shallow brooks with a stony ground covered with sand, are typical.</li><li>Consequently many cathedral organists find themselves occupied increasingly with diocesan work.</li><li>Small households that don&#x27;t use much water but occupy homes with high rateable values could be much better off.</li><li>Most hobbies cost some money, some a great deal, why not occupy time with machine knitting?</li><li>The rest of the day, she occupied herself with manufacturing chores to do.</li><li>Temporary relief from worry and anxiety can be achieved by totally occupying the mind with something else.</li><li>Over the next few weeks, Father Maier was occupied more with the political than with the priestly.</li><li>For the next four years he occupied himself primarily with writings in which he leveled attacks against enemies of the faith.</li></ul></section>

- UsageHTML: <section class="usage-box"><div class="usage-title">Register</div><div class="usage-en">Outcome is slightly formal and is used mostly in writing. In everyday English, people are more likely to talk about what happened:</div><div class="usage-cn">outcome 稍显正式，多用于书面语中。在日常英语中，人们较多使用 what happened</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">It was impossible to predict what would happen in the election.</div><div class="example-cn">这次选举的结果无法预测。</div></div></section>
- CorpusHTML: <section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">outcome</div><ul><li>The talks had a better outcome than we had originally hoped.</li><li>Qualitative judgements are then derived from the positive or negative outcome of the quantities involved.</li><li>No outcome seems too impossible or, at least, unworthy of valiant effort.</li><li>The negotiations are continuing, and we are hoping for a positive outcome.</li><li>Criteria should not be a list of every possible outcome and / or process that is a component of total care.</li><li>Then we can allow ourselves to feel subjectively good about the outcome, whatever our objective achievement.</li><li>The patient&#x27;s general health and fitness can also affect the outcome of the disease.</li><li>The campaign is still young, and the outcome could change drastically as it did four years ago.</li><li>And the outcome of all this was to go back to the basics.</li><li>At this point, I wouldn&#x27;t even try to predict the outcome, but we&#x27;re hoping for the best.</li><li>It&#x27;s impossible to say for sure what the outcome of the election will be.</li><li>Whatever the outcome, I hope we remain friends.</li><li>Which outcome is better for society?</li><li>A win-win outcome is where all parties involved are successful in achieving their objectives.</li></ul></section><section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">outcome of</div><ul><li>factors that influenced the outcome of the war</li></ul></section>

- DefinitionsHTML: <section class="pos-block"><div class="pos-title">noun <span class="homnum">1</span> <span class="pron">/ˈaʊtlaɪn/</span></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">1</span><div class="grammar">[countable C, uncountable U]</div><div class="activator">SUMMARIZE</div><div class="def-en">the main ideas or facts about something, without the details</div><div class="def-cn">纲要，梗概，要点</div><div class="patterns"><span class="label">Pattern</span> outline of · broad/rough/general outline</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">a research proposal outline</div><div class="example-cn">研究计划梗概</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">an outline of world history</div><div class="example-cn">世界史纲</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">a broad outline of the committee’s plans</div><div class="example-cn">委员会计划的一个粗略纲要</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">A debt reduction scheme was agreed in outline (= people agreed on its main points).</div><div class="example-cn">债务削减计划大致已经商定。</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">2</span><div class="grammar">[countable C, uncountable U]</div><div class="activator">SHAPE</div><div class="def-en">a line around the edge of something which shows its shape</div><div class="def-cn">外形，轮廓</div><div class="patterns"><span class="label">Pattern</span> outline of</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">The outlines of animals were cut into the rock.</div><div class="example-cn">动物轮廓被刻在岩石上。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">an outline map of Europe</div><div class="example-cn">欧洲略图</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">figures drawn in outline</div><div class="example-cn">人物的轮廓</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">3</span><div class="grammar">[countable C]</div><div class="activator">SUMMARIZE</div><div class="def-en">a plan for a piece of writing in which each new idea or fact is separately written down</div><div class="def-cn">提纲，纲要</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">Always write an outline for your essays.</div><div class="example-cn">写文章一定要先列个提纲。</div></div></div></section><section class="pos-block"><div class="pos-title">verb <span class="homnum">2</span></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">1</span><div class="activator">SUMMARIZE</div><div class="def-en">to describe something in a general way, giving the main points but not the details</div><div class="def-cn">概述；提出 … 的纲要</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">The new president outlined plans to deal with crime, drugs, and education.</div><div class="example-cn">新总统概述了解决犯罪、毒品和教育问题的计划。</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">2</span><div class="activator">SHAPE</div><div class="def-en">to show the edge of something, or draw around its edge, so that its shape is clear</div><div class="def-cn">画 … 的轮廓，描 … 的外形</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">a map with our property outlined in red</div><div class="example-cn">用红色勾画出我们住宅轮廓的地图</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">trees outlined against the sky</div><div class="example-cn">天空映衬下的树木轮廓</div></div></div></section>

- DefinitionsHTML: <section class="pos-block"><div class="pos-title">noun <span class="pron">/ˈaʊtlʊk/</span></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">1</span><div class="activator">ATTITUDE</div><div class="def-en">your general attitude to life and the world</div><div class="def-cn">〔对生活和世界的〕看法，观点，态度</div><div class="patterns"><span class="label">Pattern</span> outlook on · positive/optimistic outlook</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">He’s got a good outlook on life.</div><div class="example-cn">他有积极的人生观。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">Exercise will improve your looks and your outlook.</div><div class="example-cn">运动将会改善你的外在形象和人生态度。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">She still has an optimistic outlook for the future.</div><div class="example-cn">她对未来仍抱有乐观的态度。</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">2</span><div class="grammar">[usually singular]</div><div class="activator">FUTURE · WEATHER</div><div class="def-en">what is expected to happen in the future</div><div class="def-cn">前景，远景</div><div class="patterns"><span class="label">Pattern</span> outlook for · economic/financial/political etc outlook</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">The outlook for the weekend is unsettled, with periods of heavy rain.</div><div class="example-cn">周末的天气情况不稳定，会有阵发性的大雨。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">The outlook for sufferers from this disease is bleak.</div><div class="example-cn">这种疾病的患者痊愈的希望渺茫。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">a gloomy economic outlook in Western Europe</div><div class="example-cn">西欧惨淡的经济前景</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">3</span><div class="activator">SEE</div><div class="def-en">a view from a particular place</div><div class="def-cn">〔从某处望见的〕景色，风光</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">a very pleasing outlook from the bedroom window</div><div class="example-cn">从卧室窗户看出去的宜人景色</div></div></div></section>
- CorpusHTML: <section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">outlook</div><ul><li>Assuming this passes the Congress, it will change the defence outlook radically.</li><li>After a good vacation, you&#x27;ll have a completely different outlook.</li><li>His outlook on life is largely a result of his strict education.</li><li>Partly due to its history, and partly to temperament, the Home Office is conservative procedurally and cautious in outlook.</li><li>Because attention was focused on customers and their changing demands, the organisation became dynamic in outlook.</li><li>The airline&#x27;s negative outlook was no surprise.</li><li>Village life and the peasant outlook were conditioned by the administrative arrangements adopted at Emancipation.</li><li>Whenever Stewart showed signs of rejecting that outlook, Joe would fly into a rage.</li><li>Consumers continue to be pessimistic about the outlook over the next six months, the Conference Board said.</li><li>Deng responded optimistically that the outlook was still bright.</li><li>The farmers were narrowly provincial in their outlook.</li></ul></section><section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">positive/optimistic outlook</div><ul><li>Managers say what&#x27;s needed now is a period of calm and a positive outlook.</li><li>There is nothing likelier to give you a positive outlook on life than the cessation of nausea.</li><li>Want to build a more positive outlook.</li><li>These facts account for a more optimistic outlook of potential supply given in the 1981 report.</li><li>Then I took a more positive outlook.</li><li>That&#x27;s the optimistic outlook of Bordon businessman Philip Voice, who says he&#x27;s never had it so good.</li><li>Nearly everyone had a very positive outlook and the plans for action to revive the area were discussed.</li></ul></section><section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">economic/financial/political etc outlook</div><ul><li>In spite of a change in political outlook, the ravaging of national book treasures did not stop in the post-war era.</li><li>The people were undergoing a gradual change in political outlook.</li><li>The work led Russell himself to conclude that the teaching of the subject had no effect whatsoever on pupils &#x27; political outlook.</li><li>Around 1883 the economic outlook began to improve.</li><li>He was not too hopeful of the financial outlook which was far from satisfactory.</li></ul></section>

### owe

- POS: NOUN
- Frequency: 1
- Local word: UNMATCHED

- ID: owe
- DisplayWord: owe
- Pronunciation: verb: /əʊ/
- POS: verb
- Frequency: ●●● ; S2
- DefinitionsHTML: <section class="pos-block"><div class="pos-title">verb <span class="pron">/əʊ/</span></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">1</span><div class="activator">OWE</div><div class="def-en">to need to pay someone for something that they have done for you or sold to you, or to need to give someone back money that they have lent you</div><div class="def-cn">欠〔钱〕；负债</div><div class="patterns"><span class="label">Pattern</span> owe somebody money/£10 etc</div><div class="relations">→ borrow ·, lend</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">I owe my brother $50.</div><div class="example-cn">我欠弟弟 50 美元。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">I still owe you for the taxi.</div><div class="example-cn">我还欠你出租车费呢。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">How much do I owe you (= often used to show that you want to pay for something)?</div><div class="example-cn">我该付你多少钱？</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">the money owed to credit card companies</div><div class="example-cn">欠信用卡公司的钱</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">2</span><div class="activator">SHOULD/OUGHT TO</div><div class="def-en">to feel that you should do something for someone or give someone something, because they have done something for you or given something to you</div><div class="def-cn">应该做；应给予；对 … 负有 … 的义务</div><div class="patterns"><span class="label">Pattern</span> owe somebody a drink/letter etc</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">He asked for help from a colleague who owed him a favour.</div><div class="example-cn">他请了一个同事帮忙，那人曾欠他一个情。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">I owe Shaun a letter; I must write soon.</div><div class="example-cn">我欠肖恩一封信，我得尽快写。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">Thanks a lot for being so understanding about all this – I owe you one (= used to thank someone who has helped you, and to say that you are willing to help them in the future)!</div><div class="example-cn">非常感谢你对这一切这么理解 —— 我欠你一个人情！</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">Let’s go and see Joe – he owes me!</div><div class="example-cn">我们去找找乔看 —— 他欠我的情呢！</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">3</span><div class="phrase">owe somebody an explanation/apology</div><div class="activator">SORRY/APOLOGIZE</div><div class="def-en">to feel that you should give someone an explanation of why you did something, or say you are sorry</div><div class="def-cn">该向某人解释 / 致歉</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">You owe him an apology.</div><div class="example-cn">你应该向他道歉。</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">4</span><div class="patterns"><span class="label">Pattern</span> owe somebody a lot/owe somebody a great deal · owe it all to somebody/owe everything to somebody · owe somebody a debt (of gratitude)</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">He probably owes his life to her prompt action.</div><div class="example-cn">很可能是因为她行动迅速，才救了他一命。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">‘I owe my parents a lot, ’ he admitted.</div><div class="example-cn">“ 我非常感激我的父母。 ” 他承认道。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">He owes a great deal to his publishers.</div><div class="example-cn">他非常感激他的出版商。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">I owe it all to you.</div><div class="example-cn">这一切都多亏了你。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">the debt that we owe to our teachers</div><div class="example-cn">我们对老师们的感激之情</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">5</span><div class="activator">BECAUSE</div><div class="def-en">to be successful because of the good effect or influence of something or someone</div><div class="def-cn">归功于〔某事〕</div><div class="patterns"><span class="label">Pattern</span> owe to</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">Their success owes more to good luck than to careful management.</div><div class="example-cn">他们的成功更多靠的是好运气，而不是苦心经营。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">Pearson’s work owed much to the research of his friend, Hugh Kingsmill.</div><div class="example-cn">皮尔逊的工作成果很大程度上应该归功于他朋友休 • 金斯米尔的研究。</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">6</span><div class="phrase">owe it to somebody to do something</div><div class="activator">IMPORTANT</div><div class="def-en">to feel you should do something for someone, because they have helped you or given you support</div><div class="def-cn">〔认为〕应该为某人做某事</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">You owe it to your supporters not to give up now.</div><div class="example-cn">为了对得起你的支持者，你现在不应该放弃。</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">7</span><div class="phrase">owe it to yourself to do something</div><div class="activator">DESERVE</div><div class="def-en">to feel you should try to achieve something because it is what you deserve</div><div class="def-cn">〔认为〕自己应该做某事</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">You owe it to yourself to take some time off.</div><div class="example-cn">你该让自己休息一下了。</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">8</span><div class="phrase">owe loyalty/allegiance etc to somebody</div><div class="activator">OBEY</div><div class="def-en">to have a duty to obey someone</div><div class="def-cn">负有效忠某人的义务</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">provinces owing allegiance to the Emperor</div><div class="example-cn">必须效忠皇帝的各省</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">9</span><div class="phrase">think that the world owes you a living</div><div class="activator">LAZY</div><div class="def-en">to be unwilling to work in order to get things, and expect them to be provided for you – used to show disapproval</div><div class="def-cn">认为生来就该过舒服的日子〔含贬义〕</div></div></section>
- CorpusHTML: <section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">owe somebody an explanation/apology</div><ul><li>At the same time I felt I was owed an explanation.</li><li>I guess I owe her an apology.</li><li>I think these people who said those hateful things about him owe him an apology.</li><li>In light of this, do you feel you owe the world an apology?</li><li>Of course, a decision not to have children is a legitimate choice, and whoever makes it owes no explanation.</li><li>You owe him an apology for misjudging him and suspecting his motives at every turn.</li><li>At the very least a clear case is owed a clear explanation if it is rejected.</li><li>I think you owe an apology to Clegg.</li></ul></section><section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">owe it to somebody to do something</div><ul><li>We owe it to clarity to disentangle the varieties of suffering possible in a given situation.</li><li>We owe it to gastronomy to keep them alive.</li><li>We owe it to our children to clean up the environment.</li><li>We owe it to ourselves to consider alternative futures, based on what we know and what we can project from that.</li><li>It was a lame excuse, and I bluntly told him that he owed it to posterity to relate his story.</li><li>He owed it to Sue to avenge Arabella.</li><li>I owe it to Victoria to lend some retrospective weight to our parting.</li><li>You owe it to yourself to extract yourself from your present situation and reassess your life.</li><li>For health insurance reasons you owe it to yourself to take care of your one and only body - your working machine.</li></ul></section><section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">owe it to yourself to do something</div><ul><li>Do I owe it to myself to finish?</li><li>We owe it to ourselves to consider alternative futures, based on what we know and what we can project from that.</li><li>You owe it to yourself to extract yourself from your present situation and reassess your life.</li><li>For health insurance reasons you owe it to yourself to take care of your one and only body - - DefinitionsHTML: <section class="pos-block"><div class="pos-title">noun <span class="pron">/fɪˈnɒmənən/</span></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">1</span><div class="phrase">event</div><div class="activator">HAPPEN</div><div class="def-en">something that happens or exists in society, science, or nature, especially something that is studied because it is difficult to understand</div><div class="def-cn">现象</div><div class="patterns"><span class="label">Pattern</span> phenomenon of · natural/historical/social etc phenomenon</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">the growing phenomenon of telecommuting</div><div class="example-cn">逐渐增多的远程办公现象</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">Homelessness is not a new phenomenon.</div><div class="example-cn">无家可归已不是什么新现象。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">Language is a social and cultural phenomenon.</div><div class="example-cn">语言是一种社会文化现象。</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">2</span><div class="activator">UNUSUAL</div><div class="def-en">something or someone that is very unusual because of a rare quality or ability that they have</div><div class="def-cn">非凡的人 [事物] ；奇才；奇事</div></div></section>
- CorpusHTML: <section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">phenomenon</div><ul><li>Still walking five miles a day at the age of 95, the woman was an absolute phenomenon.</li><li>He is yet another phenomenon of questionable tangibility to emerge from the twelfth century.</li><li>the increasing phenomenon of the single parent family</li><li>Then an interesting phenomenon takes place: they become a safety valve.</li><li>Is it an illusion to imagine that this is a merely modern phenomenon? he wrote.</li><li>A new phenomenon is identified in some prisons.</li><li>Industrial ReD in the public sector is a relatively new phenomenon and the expectations from it are not very clear.</li><li>In dealing with this new phenomenon, I have two points to make.</li><li>The cell phone is a relatively recent phenomenon. It&#x27;s difficult at the moment to assess its effects.</li><li>The same phenomenon was observed in New York.</li><li>We now know that our system of planets orbiting the sun is not a unique phenomenon.</li></ul></section><section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">phenomenon of</div><ul><li>the phenomenon of international terrorism</li></ul></section>

- DefinitionsHTML: <section class="pos-block"><div class="pos-title">noun <span class="pron">/fəˈlɒsəfi/</span></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">1</span><div class="grammar">[uncountable U]</div><div class="def-en">the study of the nature and meaning of existence, truth, good and evil etc</div><div class="def-cn">哲学</div><div class="patterns"><span class="label">Pattern</span> philosophy of</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">Emma studies philosophy at university.</div><div class="example-cn">埃玛在大学攻读哲学。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">the philosophy of science</div><div class="example-cn">科学哲学</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">2</span><div class="grammar">[countable C]</div><div class="def-en">the views of a particular philosopher or group of philosophers</div><div class="def-cn">思想体系；哲学体系</div><div class="patterns"><span class="label">Pattern</span> philosophy of</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">the philosophy of Aristotle</div><div class="example-cn">亚里士多德的哲学体系</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">3</span><div class="grammar">[countable C]</div><div class="activator">BELIEVE</div><div class="def-en">the attitude or set of ideas that guides the behaviour of a person or organization</div><div class="def-cn">人生哲学；生活 [工作] 准则</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">The company explained their management philosophy.</div><div class="example-cn">公司阐述了他们的管理原则。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">The idea that you should treat others as you would like them to treat you is a fine philosophy of life.</div><div class="example-cn">希望别人怎样对你，你就怎样对待别人，这是很好的处世原则。</div></div></div></section>
- CorpusHTML: <section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">philosophy</div><ul><li>Eastern religions and philosophies</li><li>They had a different philosophy, one that she really believed in.</li><li>No longer does our political process discuss philosophy and issues.</li><li>My philosophy is, I leave work at 5 o&#x27;clock and forget all about it till the next day.</li><li>Our production philosophy requires all operations to be safe, and we apply innovative techniques alongside proven technology.</li><li>the philosophy of Nietzsche</li><li>In many ways, their philosophy was similar to that which guided Loeb and his successors.</li><li>Piaget moved from biology to philosophy and eventually to psychology early in his life.</li></ul></section><section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">philosophy of life</div><ul><li>Unity is a, sort of like a philosophy of life, sort of.</li><li>Everybody shared a philosophy of life as basic as the soil and as obvious as the sky.</li><li>These men often have similar backgrounds and philosophies of life which lead to similar results and successes.</li><li>In fact, they later changed my philosophy of life.</li><li>Finally, the drawing is ongoing and never finished, which one could say reflects one of my philosophies of life.</li><li>We often discussed our work, our so-called careers and our philosophies of life, such as they were.</li><li>The wonderfully spontaneous mortgage department was the place to be if your philosophy of life was: Ready, fire, aim.</li></ul></section>

- CorpusHTML: <section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">pilgrimage</div><ul><li>They set out for a pilgrimage to Rome.</li><li>On his recovery he made a pilgrimage to the shrine of Rocamadour in the Quercy.</li><li>Today, Dominique Sennelier, third-generation director of the prestigious company, makes a pilgrimage to Tucson.</li><li>It was sort of a pilgrimage.</li><li>It was a pilgrimage I had had to make, and I was glad I had made it.</li><li>a pilgrimage to Graceland, Elvis&#x27; home</li><li>a pilgrimage to Mecca</li><li>In March, the Lowes made their annual pilgrimage to the Rockies.</li><li>I made two more visits to Knowlton, and it has now become a focus for my own particular pilgrimage.</li><li>I am walking the river from mouth to source, ending my journey at Amarkantak-only half the pilgrimage.</li><li>Each arises in a special way in the pilgrimage toward a united church.</li></ul></section><section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">place of pilgrimage</div><ul><li>Klingenzell priory, between the castles Liebenfels and Freudenfels, was founded in 1333 and became a place of pilgrimage.</li><li>Gwytherin became a place of pilgrimage to followers of her cult.</li><li>His presence has already made Gyuto a place of pilgrimage.</li><li>That aspect of Lourdes is now of course utterly dominant: this is a place of pilgrimage and little else.</li><li>It was once a place of pilgrimage for local people, who came to listen to the nightingales that nested here.</li><li>There, in 612, he established his hermitage, which was soon a place of pilgrimage.</li><li>It, too, is an important place of pilgrimage and its music is increasingly finding its way into parishes.</li><li>I have made places of pilgrimage. and cared for their pilgrims.</li></ul></section>

- DefinitionsHTML: <section class="pos-block"><div class="pos-title">noun <span class="pron">/ˈpleɪdʒərɪzəm/</span></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">1</span><div class="grammar">[uncountable U]</div><div class="activator">COPY</div><div class="def-en">when someone uses another person’s words, ideas, or work and pretends they are their own</div><div class="def-cn">剽窃，抄袭</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">The journal accused the professor of plagiarism.</div><div class="example-cn">那份刊物指控该教授剽窃。</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">2</span><div class="grammar">[countable C]</div><div class="activator">COPY</div><div class="def-en">an idea, phrase, or story that has been copied from another person’s work, without stating where it came from</div><div class="def-cn">剽窃物</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">claims that there are plagiarisms in the new software</div><div class="example-cn">声称新软件有剽窃之处</div></div></div></section>
- CorpusHTML: <section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">plagiarism</div><ul><li>Does the student follow the old adage that to read and paraphrase one book is plagiarism but to use two is research?</li><li>His dissertation contained many plagiarisms.</li><li>Claims of plagiarism are common in the movie business.</li><li>She cobbled together a rough draft and then rewrote it, trying to remove the more ostentatious signs of plagiarism.</li><li>The Head of Department in consultation with the Dean is responsible for recommending appropriate action in cases of suspected cheating or plagiarism by students.</li><li>The system was designed to prevent plagiarism, and to establish copyright over the thesis contents.</li><li>There are all sorts of coincidences which are in no way plagiarism.</li></ul></section>

- CorpusHTML: <section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">what possessed somebody (to do something)?</div><ul><li>I don&#x27;t know what possessed me to buy such an ugly dress.</li></ul></section><section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">possess</div><ul><li>Because of his gambling, he lost everything he possessed.</li><li>Hamly admitted illegally possessing a handgun.</li><li>The Western Highlands possess a beauty and a majesty found nowhere else in Britain.</li><li>The Church possesses a bone from the saint&#x27;s leg.</li><li>Lipatti s performance possesses a clarity of articulation, a depth of sonority and an energy that shine through the crackly recording.</li><li>Like all towns and villages on Trinidad, it possessed a cricket ground.</li><li>Japetus alone possessed a distinctive geography, and a very strange one indeed.</li><li>Very few families in this area possess a telephone.</li><li>He possessed an unusual ability to learn languages quickly.</li><li>Too many nations already possess chemical weapons.</li><li>But with only two characters you can&#x27;t hope to control everything, or claim to possess every solution.</li><li>Jo believed that demons possessed her.</li><li>A sense of fear possessed him as he walked into the old house.</li><li>Zorna is said to possess miraculous healing powers.</li><li>The number of nations that possess nuclear weapons has risen.</li><li>Let us assume that the entire being is possessed of 1,000 arbitrary units of life force.</li><li>He never wore a suit - I don&#x27;t think he possessed one.</li><li>If a child is learning at grade level, by definition he or she must possess reasonably good intellectual abilities.</li><li>The rhetorical theorist does not assume that only some societies possess the rhetorical capacity to argue.</li><li>The caller claimed to possess valuable information about the boy&#x27;s whereabouts.</li></ul></section>

Koch&#x27;s postulates would of course be unethical and controversy is fuelled by this lack of scientific certainty.</li><li>Here Moscovici is offering a universal postulate about social psychological processes.</li></ul></section>

- CorpusHTML: <section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">predilection</div><ul><li>Lacking the certainty that arises from inner, mystic experience, we have a predilection to replace genuine knowledge with dogma.</li><li>He is a grammarian, a swordsman, a musician with a predilection for the fugue.</li><li>Petitioner certainly was not attempting to conceal or withhold from the Committee his own past political associations, predilections, and preferences.</li><li>In fact, there seems to be a general predilection of benign strictures for the left side of the colon.</li><li>Those who knew of his predilections often wondered why he had not become a botanist, an entomologist, a biologist.</li><li>Spark has always had the facility to be silkily suave as she goes about examining our predilection for worshipping false gods.</li><li>This supposition becomes more likely in light of Hamann&#x27;s predilection for parables as the most appropriate genre for telling the truth.</li><li>So the predilections of beavers centuries ago may well have determined the places where human beings have their towns today.</li></ul></section>
- OriginHTML: <div class="origin">predilection (1700-1800) French prédilection, from Medieval Latin praediligere “ to love more, prefer ”, from Latin diligere; → DILIGENT</div>

- CorpusHTML: <section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">preference</div><ul><li>When they&#x27;re old enough for a preference, he&#x27;s the preference.</li><li>Coupons generated preference for lower temperatures, this is an ideal plant for the garden pool.</li><li>Most of us arrange our bedrooms based purely on personal preference.</li><li>Our personal preference is to cook hotel to tailor service preferences for each guest.</li><li>When he provided nests on two tiers, hens showed a strong preference for the lower level.</li><li>Oil or vinegar may be added for a more firms to expand their own internal capacity in preference to extensive reliance on outside suppliers.</li><li>I like paying with credit cards in preference to cash.</li><li>These factors also influence the demand for one sort of drink in preference to another.</li><li>Therefore, it seems shareholders should absorb the risks of an enterprise in preference to management doing so.</li><li>The victims of a burglary are often puzzled as to why the thief chose their home in preference to others.</li><li>Experiment also shows that the eye learns to travel along the upper edge of a line in preference to the lower edge.</li><li>Secondly, there are processes which select certain patterns of motion in preference to others.</li><li>The idea of anybody, Marge especially, liking that wall-eyed ox in preference to Dickie made Tom smile.</li><li>There are certain clothes we feel comfortable in and which we would wear in preference to all others.</li></ul></section><section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">give/show preference (to somebody)</div><ul><li>Similarly, infants as young as 6 weeks of age consistently show preferences for familiar as compared to unfamiliar faces.</li><li>For example, there have already been reports of hospitals giving preference to patients of fundholding general practitioners.</li><li>It is blatant, undisguised opportunism by management, showing preference for what can be done, rather than what should be done.</li><li>To the extent that rank-ordering means giving preferences to candidates of one party rather than another it is both easy and reasonable.</li><li>Flaggers will direct traffic, giving preference to northbound traffic in the morning and southbound in the evening.</li></ul></section>

- DefinitionsHTML: <section class="pos-block"><div class="pos-title">noun <span class="pron">/priːˌɒkjəˈpeɪʃən/</span></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">1</span><div class="grammar">[singular, uncountable U]</div><div class="activator">INTERESTED</div><div class="def-en">when someone thinks or worries about something a lot, with the result that they do not pay attention to other things</div><div class="def-cn">全神贯注；入神</div><div class="patterns"><span class="label">Pattern</span> preoccupation with</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">the current preoccupation with sex and scandal</div><div class="example-cn">目前大家对性和丑闻的高度关注</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">The management’s preoccupation with costs and profits resulted in a drop in quality and customer service.</div><div class="example-cn">管理层过于追求成本效益和利润，导致产品质量和客户服务水平有所下降。</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">2</span><div class="grammar">[countable C]</div><div class="activator">OBSESSION</div><div class="def-en">something that you give all your attention to</div><div class="def-cn">使人全神贯注的事物，使人入神的事物</div><div class="patterns"><span class="label">Pattern</span> main/chief/central etc preoccupation</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">Their main preoccupation was how to feed their families.</div><div class="example-cn">他们主要关心的是如何养家糊口。</div></div></div></section>
- CorpusHTML: <section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">preoccupation</div><ul><li>Richards found a preoccupation amongst employers with the image of engineering.</li><li>And increasingly, the relatively brief preoccupation with methodology was seen to have run its course in economics.</li><li>In her hands she carried two things that made Creusa, in all her preoccupation, start and look sharply at them.</li><li>Linear preoccupation in the past remains a closed book to modern understanding.</li><li>Brad&#x27;s main preoccupations were eating and sleeping.</li><li>A major preoccupation of writers on organization has been the design of structures that will maximize efficiency.</li><li>Music has been his major preoccupation since childhood.</li><li>Politics became the major preoccupation shared by all, rather than the concern of the ruling few.</li><li>Writing a will is not evidence of a morbid preoccupation with death.</li><li>Georgina&#x27;s preoccupation with her appearance takes up most of her time.</li><li>In any case, the argument was quite remote from Lenin&#x27;s preoccupation with binding up the wounds of national estrangement.</li></ul></section><section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">preoccupation with</div><ul><li>Rockburne&#x27;s new paintings show her preoccupation with color and measurement.</li></ul></section><section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">main/chief/central etc preoccupation</div><ul><li>Pay flexibility is a main preoccupation of Mr Montagu and Mr Brown in the planning stage.</li><li>The national question as such still remains a central preoccupation for catholic nationalists.</li><li>A sleepless alien might legitimately conclude that Earthlings &#x27; central preoccupation was this peculiar sort of inactivity.</li><li>But his main preoccupation was with the unfinished Requiem, which had begun to prey on his mind.</li><li>That was even true of de Gaulle&#x27;s other main preoccupation in these years - his ambitious and contentious foreign policy.</li><li>Mr Reynolds&#x27; main preoccupation before his operation is with the stoma which will be formed during the procedure.</li><li>When at home, Mr Berisha&#x27;s main preoccupation is keeping his unruly party under control.</li><li>Power was the chief preoccupation of Lenin and Stalin.</li></ul></section>

- DefinitionsHTML: <section class="pos-block"><div class="pos-title">noun <span class="pron">/ˌprezəˈveɪʃən/</span></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">1</span><div class="activator">CONTINUE/NOT STOP</div><div class="def-en">when something is kept in its original state or in good condition</div><div class="def-cn">保存；保护</div><div class="patterns"><span class="label">Pattern</span> preservation of</div><div class="relations">→ preserve</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">Eliot campaigned for the preservation of London’s churches.</div><div class="example-cn">埃利奥特发起了保护伦敦各教堂的运动。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">We are working for the preservation of the environment.</div><div class="example-cn">我们正致力于环境保护工作。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">the preservation of our cultural heritage</div><div class="example-cn">对我们文化遗产的保护</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">methods of food preservation</div><div class="example-cn">保存食物的各种方法</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">2</span><div class="def-en">the act of making sure that a situation continues without changing</div><div class="def-cn">维护；保护；保持，维持</div><div class="patterns"><span class="label">Pattern</span> preservation of</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">the preservation of peace in the region</div><div class="example-cn">维护该地区的和平</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">3</span><div class="activator">CHANGE/BECOME DIFFERENT</div><div class="def-en">the degree to which something has remained unchanged or unharmed by weather, age etc</div><div class="def-cn">保存的状况</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">The arena is in an exceptionally fine state of preservation.</div><div class="example-cn">那座竞技场保存得非常完好。</div></div></div></section>

getting a job would give him his pride back.</div><div class="example-cn">我认为找份工作可以让他重拾自尊。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">She didn’t try to hide her anger and injured class="example-cn">对某些男人来说妻子无需工作是关乎自尊的事。</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">3</span><div class="grammar">[uncountable U]</div><div class="activator">PROUD</div><div - CorpusHTML: <section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">prominent</div><ul><li>His face was tanned, the cheekbones high and prominent.</li><li>The conference was attended by both government officials and prominent academics.</li><li>Her nose was quite prominent, and she had small, even teeth.</li><li>It is marked by the three prominent black stripes.</li><li>Her short wavy black hair was combed neatly back from a rather narrow sloping forehead with prominent brow ridges.</li><li>a prominent business leader</li><li>In the process the owners themselves became prominent community leaders and among the biggest advertisers in the emerging gay press.</li><li>Politicians who are prominent in public life may be at risk from terrorism.</li><li>Daguerre was a prominent Mexico City lawyer.</li><li>Rheme position, on the other hand, is prominent on an overall discourse level.</li><li>The housing needs of the elderly, in particular, must be a prominent policy issue in years to come.</li><li>Yet there were other new ideas that jostled together in his brain for some more prominent recognition.</li><li>Their contentions are supported by several prominent researchers.</li><li>a heart-shaped face, slightly prominent teeth and small eyes</li><li>Martelli and Bettino Craxi, ex-leader of the Socialists are among its most prominent victims.</li></ul></section><section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">prominent place</div><ul><li>The Phillips curve gets a prominent place, but so do its limitations.</li><li>This matter ought to occupy a prominent place in the Election Manifesto.</li><li>The issue of censorship took a prominent place in the seminar discussions.</li><li>Housing occupies a prominent place in these debates.</li><li>In Sri Lanka&#x27;s constitution a very prominent place is given to the Buddhist religion.</li><li>Don&#x27;t enter the firing ranges when the red flags are flying - usually from prominent places such as hilltops.</li><li>In our wishful thinking about the 1960s, no figures occupy a more prominent place than the Kennedys.</li><li>The popular daily press in the Edwardian years began to give quite a prominent place to sport.</li></ul></section><section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">prominent place/position</div><ul><li>Now there is talk of recruiting blacks and Latinos, traditionally absent from the higher union ranks, to more prominent positions.</li><li>The cars were painted khaki with the red cross in a prominent position.</li><li>The Phillips curve gets a prominent place, but so do its limitations.</li><li>This year I bedded out a few of these house plants in a prominent position in the garden.</li><li>Further, public response to works in prominent positions is rarely commented on.</li><li>Wexford found the lead, obligingly left by Sheila in a prominent position on top of the refrigerator.</li><li>In our wishful thinking about the 1960s, no figures occupy a more prominent place than the Kennedys.</li><li>The popular daily press in the Edwardian years began to give quite a prominent place to sport.</li></ul></section>

- DefinitionsHTML: <section class="pos-block"><div class="pos-title">noun <span class="pron">/pəˈsjuːt/</span></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">1</span><div class="grammar">[uncountable U]</div><div class="activator">DO</div><div class="def-en">when someone tries to get, achieve, or find something in a determined way</div><div class="def-cn">追求；寻找</div><div class="patterns"><span class="label">Pattern</span> pursuit of</div><div class="relations">→ pursue</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">the pursuit of liberty and happiness</div><div class="example-cn">对自由和幸福的追求</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">the pursuit of war criminals</div><div class="example-cn">追踪战犯</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">People are having to move to other areas in pursuit of work.</div><div class="example-cn">为了找工作，人们不得不移居他处。</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">2</span><div class="grammar">[uncountable U]</div><div class="activator">FOLLOW</div><div class="def-en">when someone chases or follows someone else</div><div class="def-cn">追赶，追踪</div><div class="relations">→ pursue</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">There were four police cars in pursuit.</div><div class="example-cn">有四辆警车在追赶。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">The quarterback sprinted toward the end zone with Jansen in hot pursuit (= following closely behind).</div><div class="example-cn">那名四分卫快速冲向底线区，詹森穷追不舍。</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">3</span><div class="grammar">[countable C usually plural]</div><div class="register">formal</div><div class="activator">DO</div><div class="def-en">an activity such as a sport or hobby, which you spend a lot of time doing</div><div class="def-cn">消遣；嗜好，爱好</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">pursuits such as swimming and tennis</div><div class="example-cn">游泳和打网球之类的爱好</div></div></div></section>
- CorpusHTML: <section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">pursuit</div><ul><li>Gentle took a moment to ask if Judith was all right - which she was - then raced in pursuit.</li><li>The Confederates, their own ranks disorganized and in a state of confusion, made only a limited pursuit.</li><li>Science is a logical pursuit but progress in science does not necessarily, or even usually, follow a straight path.</li><li>Moriarty spent the summer focusing on his musical pursuits.</li><li>I learned something about the difference between a serious and quiet pursuit and a popular movement.</li><li>His aristocratic family was so against his religious pursuits they locked him away for fifteen months.</li><li>But it is likely that both would be harder-nosed in the pursuit of national interests.</li><li>Furthermore, he is only concerned with one thing and that is the pursuit of the White Whale.</li><li>In a traditional adventure story the pursuit of personal honour is drawn to an absolute conclusion.</li></ul></section><section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">pursuit of</div><ul><li>the pursuit of truth and justice</li></ul></section><section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">in pursuit</div><ul><li>The suspect crossed the bridge, with four police cars in pursuit.</li><li>A deer suddenly sprang across the road, with a pack of hunting dogs in hot pursuit.</li><li>Cheng raced through a crowded shopping mall in pursuit of the man who had grabbed her purse.</li><li>The robbers sped off in a stolen car with three police vehicles in pursuit.</li></ul></section>

- CorpusHTML: <section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">refusal</div><ul><li>Refusal to do military service was a criminal offence.</li><li>It is a restlessness, a refusal to longterm relationships, that has typified both his public and private life.</li><li>There was an association between refusal and having a younger sibling.</li><li>His request for a bigger room met with a blunt refusal.</li><li>There&#x27;d been a chorus of objection then and a flat refusal from Becky to stay with the younger children.</li><li>He was upset by her refusal.</li><li>She must understand the consequences of her refusal to accept medical treatment.</li><li>Kelly Johnson was a curmudgeon, but he was revered at the Skunk Works for his refusal to compromise about airplanes.</li><li>The great imperial Zanuck was not amused at Boyo Burton&#x27;s refusal and tried to force his hand.</li><li>His argument seemed to be based fearlessly on the refusal to recognise what is already public knowledge about our plans.</li></ul></section><section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">refusal to do something</div><ul><li>Certainly we need to fear a refusal to change our ways.</li><li>Some people&#x27;s sensation of disbelief extends into a refusal to think about their illness at all.</li><li>Remember that it is not only a refusal to perform your normal duties which can amount to gross misconduct.</li><li>A refusal to cede two weeks of winter to the dark forces of routine.</li><li>Also prohibited is any refusal to engage meaningfully with the opponent.</li><li>His refusal to forswear moonshine, however, mocked her with the most painful failure of all.</li><li>Britain was not entirely alone in its refusal to become involved in the Schuman plan.</li><li>Mitterrand and Lecanuet portrayed the General&#x27;s refusal to campaign as contempt for the democratic process.</li><li>Samuelson&#x27;s refusal to take a drug test cost him his job.</li></ul></section>

- DefinitionsHTML: <section class="pos-block"><div class="pos-title">noun <span class="homnum">1</span> <span class="pron">/rɪˈɡɑːd/</span></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">1</span><div class="example-en">Paul seemed to regard sex as sinful and immoral.</div><div class="example-cn">保罗好像把性视为罪恶和不道德的。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">Edith was widely regarded as - DefinitionsHTML: <section class="pos-block"><div class="pos-title">verb <span class="pron">/ˌriːhəˈbɪlɪteɪt/</span></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">1</span><div class="def-en">to help someone to live a healthy, useful, or active life again after they have been seriously ill or in prison</div><div class="def-cn">协助〔重病患者〕康复；帮助〔刑满释放者〕恢复正常生活</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">a special unit for rehabilitating stroke patients</div><div class="example-cn">协助中风患者康复的特殊病房</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">2</span><div class="activator">GOOD ENOUGH</div><div class="def-en">to make people think that someone or something is good again after a period when people had a bad opinion of them</div><div class="def-cn">恢复 … 的名誉</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">The prime minister seems to be trying to rehabilitate the former defence secretary.</div><div class="example-cn">首相似乎在努力为前国防大臣恢复名誉。</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">3</span><div class="activator">IMPROVE</div><div class="def-en">to improve a building or area so that it returns to the good condition it was in before</div><div class="def-cn">使恢复原状，修复〔建筑或地区〕</div><div class="relations">→ renovate</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">A lot of the older houses have now been rehabilitated.</div><div class="example-cn">很多老房子现在都进行了修葺。</div></div></div></section>

- CorpusHTML: <section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">resign yourself to (doing) something</div><ul><li>Lydia was resigning herself to a long stretch of celibacy.</li><li>Adair, who his position on the board.</li><li>The manager was forced to resign his post after allegations of corruption.</li><li>He will resign if he is forced to accept an unrealistic budget he can not commit to.</li><li>In a statement issued on March 19 Hekmatyar called on Najibullah to resign immediately.</li><li>Former science minister Binyamin Begin, who resigned the post this week because of the wait-and-negotiate camp, Secretary of State Vance resigned his post in protest.</li><li>Bourne resigned his post over a controversy involving a prescription he wrote for a member of his staff.</li></ul></section>

- DefinitionsHTML: <section class="pos-block"><div class="pos-title">verb <span class="pron">/rɪˈteɪn/</span> <span class="register">formal</span></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">1</span><div class="activator">KEEP/CONTINUE TO HAVE</div><div class="def-en">to keep something or continue to have something</div><div class="def-cn">保留，保有；继续拥有</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">You have the right to retain possession of the goods.</div><div class="example-cn">你有权保留这些物品。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">The state wants to retain control of food imports.</div><div class="example-cn">政府想保留对食品进口的控制权。</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">2</span><div class="def-en">to store or keep something inside something else</div><div class="def-cn">保存，储存</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">A lot of information can be retained in your computer.</div><div class="example-cn">电脑可以储存很多信息。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">Limestone is known to retain moisture.</div><div class="example-cn">人们知道石灰岩能储存水分。</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">3</span><div class="def-en">to remember information</div><div class="def-cn">记住</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">I find it very difficult to retain facts.</div><div class="example-cn">我觉得具体事实很难记住。</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">4</span><div class="activator">PAY FOR</div><div class="def-en">if you retain a lawyer or other specialist, you pay them to work for you now and in the future</div><div class="def-cn">聘请〔律师、专家〕</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">He has retained a lawyer to challenge the court’s decision.</div><div class="example-cn">他聘请了一名律师质疑法庭的判决。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">We had to pay a retaining fee (= an amount of money to keep class="example-cn">招聘和留住优秀员工越来越难。</div></div></div></section>
- UsageHTML: <section class="usage-box"><div class="usage-title">Register</div><div class="usage-en">In everyday English, people usually say keep rather than retain:</div><div class="usage-cn">在日常英语中，人们一般说 keep ，而不说 retain</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">Keep all your receipts.</div><div class="example-cn">请保留所有的收据。</div></div></section>
- CorpusHTML: <section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">retain</div><ul><li>It&#x27;s important that you retain a sense of proportion when you&#x27;re feeling depressed.</li><li>For some one who worked in what she believed to be such a hard-nosed profession he retained a sensitive streak.</li><li>The treaty would not allow any country to produce, acquire, or retain chemical weapons.</li><li>It is suggested that you retain copies of the documents for at least three years.</li><li>Robertson retained his post as Minister of Information.</li><li>If a symbol does not symbolize what one thinks good or true, there can be no reason to retain it.</li><li>It retained its pot-shape although the pot was gone.</li><li>Children would retain more if the summer vacation were shorter.</li><li>The town has retained much of its country charm.</li><li>Only four members of the original marketing team will be retained next year.</li><li>Florian&#x27;s relatives will retain rights to the property.</li><li>Schools around the state say they&#x27;re having a hard time attracting and retaining teachers, especially in certain fields.</li><li>The new design will be more modern, while retaining the graceful shape of the original.</li><li>However, some have retained the more traditional method of charging commission on transactions only.</li><li>The Commission retains the services of consultants in specialized fields.</li><li>The rims of the eyes also have this same bright blue, and they retain this coloration in the adult stage.</li></ul></section>

- DefinitionsHTML: <section class="pos-block"><div class="pos-title">noun <span class="pron">/rɪˈvɪʒən/</span></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">1</span><div class="grammar">[countable C, uncountable U]</div><div class="activator">CHANGE/MAKE something DIFFERENT</div><div class="def-en">the process of changing something in order to improve it by correcting it or including new information or ideas</div><div class="def-cn">修改，修正；修订，校订</div><div class="patterns"><span class="label">Pattern</span> revision of · revision to</div><div class="relations">→ amendment</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">The judge wants to see a revision of the procedures.</div><div class="example-cn">法官希望对程序进行修改。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">I’m making some revisions to the book for the new edition.</div><div class="example-cn">我正在对这本书进行修订，准备出新版。</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">2</span><div class="grammar">[countable C]</div><div class="def-en">a piece of writing that has been improved and corrected</div><div class="def-cn">修订稿</div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">3</span><div class="grammar">[uncountable U]</div><div class="activator">STUDY</div><div class="def-en">the work of studying facts again in order to learn them</div><div class="def-cn">复习，温习</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">I know I haven’t done enough revision for tomorrow’s exam.</div><div class="example-cn">我知道我对明天的考试准备不足。</div></div></div></section>
- CorpusHTML: <section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">revision</div><ul><li>A revision to the financing element is expected in the next cou ple of years.</li><li>The second dimension implies the need for self-conscious implementation of equal opportunities and the questioning and revision of routine practices.</li><li>It is a decision that may require continual revision.</li><li>How is your history revision going?</li><li>I can&#x27;t come out tonight - I&#x27;ve got a lot of revision to do.</li><li>I&#x27;ve written the article, but it needs a lot of revision.</li><li>Others need several revisions to their surgeries, and develop painful masses of scar tissue.</li><li>The book went through several revisions before the publisher was finally satisfied with it.</li><li>These amendments constitute the most significant revision of U.S. asylum law since the Refugee Act of 1980.</li><li>In every pedagogical grammar, there should be a plan for systematic revision of previously taught material.</li><li>In order that the scheme remains popular, it is vital that revision is conducted with regard to users &#x27; needs.</li><li>Seventeen times, revision after revision, it kept coming back.</li><li>The city&#x27;s general development plan is undergoing revision.</li><li>Make sure your revisions are improvements, not just changes.</li></ul></section>

did would ever satisfy my father.</div><div class="example-cn">我做什么都不能让父亲满意。</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">2</span><div class="def-en">if you satisfy someone’s needs, class="example-cn">这一课程是为满足成年学习者的需要而设计的。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">A salad won’t be enough to satisfy my appetite.</div><div class="example-cn">一份色拉是不够让我吃饱的。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">Just to satisfy my curiosity (= find out something), how much did it cost?</div><div class="example-cn">我只是好奇想问一下，这花了多少钱？</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">3</span><div class="register">formal</div><div class="activator">PERSUADE</div><div class="def-en">to make someone feel sure that something is right or true</div><div class="def-cn">使确信，使信服</div><div class="relations">SYN convince</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">Jackson tried to satisfy me of his innocence.</div><div class="example-cn">杰克逊试图让我相信他是清白的。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">Having satisfied herself that no one was there, she closed the door.</div><div class="example-cn">她确信那里没人，就把门关上了。</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">4</span><div class="register">formal</div><div class="activator">GOOD ENOUGH</div><div class="def-en">to be good enough for a particular purpose, standard etc</div><div class="def-cn">符合，达到〔要求、标准等〕</div><div class="relations">SYN meet</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">Have you satisfied all the requirements for the general degree?</div><div class="example-cn">你达到普通学位的所有要求了吗？</div></div></div></section>
- CorpusHTML: <section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">satisfy</div><ul><li>The changes I made seemed to satisfy Cooley.</li><li>A compromise was eventually reached, but even this failed to satisfy environmentalists.</li><li>I tried on dozens of wedding dresses before I found one that satisfied me.</li><li>The cheapest products satisfy only minimum safety requirements.</li><li>We&#x27;ve already satisfied ourselves that it was an accident.</li><li>Applicants will have to satisfy the committee that they are suitable for the job.</li><li>What numbers will satisfy the equation 2 x + 3 &gt;13?</li><li>Her explanation failed to satisfy the jury.</li><li>In addition more detailed information is obtained on occasion in order to satisfy the needs of adhoc detailed projects.</li><li>When the others had satisfied their hunger he led the attack.</li><li>The police said that they were satisfied with his story and let him go free.</li></ul></section><section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">satisfy... curiosity</div><ul><li>At least he had satisfied his curiosity.</li><li>Foucard had once gone to that door, thrown it wide, given the room an all-embracing glance, satisfied his curiosity.</li><li>If this is true, it seems an expensive way of satisfying one&#x27;s curiosity.</li><li>Some came to seek the new power, some to chuckle, others to satisfy their curiosity.</li><li>Some of them I had never seen before and some were there to satisfy their curiosity.</li><li>We too need to read the Bible in our hearts, rather than simply to discover facts or satisfy our curiosity.</li><li>You still haven&#x27;t satisfied my curiosity.</li><li>If you want to satisfy your curiosity about Bob&#x27;s girlfriend, you ring him yourself.</li></ul></section><section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">satisfy yourself (that)</div><ul><li>All we had to do now was satisfy ourselves that there was enough wreckage to warrant returning for a full-scale excavation.</li><li>No-one moved until she had quite satisfied herself.</li><li>She satisfied herself by pausing on the way to the conference to score it out.</li><li>He must therefore satisfy himself on a regular basis that it does not constitute a statutory nuisance.</li><li>Decision makers should satisfy themselves that current practice is itself worth having before using it as a comparison for a new treatment.</li><li>One of these has not yet been published, so people are unable to satisfy themselves that its design is appropriate.</li><li>He decided against buying a ticket there and then but satisfied himself with getting a list of trains to Rome.</li><li>I satisfied myself with the knowledge that I would suffer far more from leaving him than he would suffer from my absence.</li></ul></section><section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">satisfied... requirements</div><ul><li>On 23 April 1991, information which satisfied the requirements of two of the four precepts in issue was produced.</li></ul></section>

- DefinitionsHTML: <section class="pos-block"><div class="pos-title">adverb <span class="pron">/ˈskeəsli/</span></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">1</span><div class="activator">JUST/ALMOST NOT</div><div class="def-en">almost not or almost none at all</div><div class="def-cn">几乎不，几乎没有</div><div class="patterns"><span class="label">Pattern</span> scarcely a day/year/moment etc</div><div class="relations">SYN hardly</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">The city had scarcely changed in 20 years.</div><div class="example-cn">这座城市 20 年中几乎没有什么改变。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">The country had scarcely any industry.</div><div class="example-cn">该国几乎没有工业。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">He scarcely ever left the region.</div><div class="example-cn">他几乎没有离开过这个地区。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">It was getting dark and she could scarcely see in front of her.</div><div class="example-cn">天色越来越黑，她几乎看不见眼前的东西。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">Scarcely a day goes by when I don’t think of him.</div><div class="example-cn">我几乎没有一天不想到他。</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">2</span><div class="activator">JUST/A MOMENT AGO</div><div class="def-en">only a moment ago</div><div class="def-cn">仅仅，刚刚</div><div class="relations">SYN hardly ·, barely</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">He had scarcely sat down when there was a knock at the door.</div><div class="example-cn">他刚坐下就有人敲门。</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">3</span><div class="activator">CERTAINLY/DEFINITELY#</div><div class="def-en">definitely not or almost certainly not</div><div class="def-cn">决不，一定不</div><div class="relations">SYN hardly</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">Early March is scarcely the time of year for sailing.</div><div class="example-cn">三月初可不是帆船运动的季节。</div></div></div></section>
- CorpusHTML: <section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">scarcely</div><ul><li>We&#x27;ve seen scarcely a drop of rain for over six months.</li><li>There can scarcely be any doubt that Sullivan is guilty.</li><li>Mutual deference could scarcely be carried farther.</li><li>It can scarcely be imagined that he would have opposed the Philadelphia Museum&#x27;s immensely well-conceived plan.</li><li>I have scarcely been myself since and I almost hate the sight of a gun.</li><li>He awoke, and it seemed that he had scarcely closed his eyes.</li><li>It was like striking gold or falling rapturously in love: he possessed secret knowledge that his Germantown friends could scarcely imagine.</li><li>I scarcely notice that my feet are cold and wet.</li><li>They sat at one of the marble-topped tables and ordered coffee from a bored waitress who scarcely spared them a glance.</li><li>They were scarcely two hundred yards distant; yet such was the gloom that they could not be clearly distinguished.</li></ul></section><section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">scarcely a day/year/moment etc</div><ul><li>He was scarcely a year older than her, but proud like a fully grown man and immensely considerate.</li><li>Matthew had been at the Plaza for a week now, with scarcely a moment to call his own.</li></ul></section>

- DefinitionsHTML: <section class="pos-block"><div class="pos-title">noun <span class="pron">/sɪˈkluːʒən/</span></div><div class="sense"><div class="grammar">[uncountable U]</div><div class="activator">SEPARATE</div><div class="def-en">the state of being private and away from other people</div><div class="def-cn">与世隔绝，隐居</div><div class="patterns"><span class="label">Pattern</span> seclusion of</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">They enjoyed ten days of peace and seclusion.</div><div class="example-cn">他们享受了十天与世隔绝的宁静生活。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">He preferred to stay at home in seclusion.</div><div class="example-cn">他更喜欢安安静静地在家里待着。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">the relative seclusion of the Norfolk countryside</div><div class="example-cn">诺福克郡乡间相对的清静</div></div></div></section>
- CorpusHTML: <section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">seclusion</div><ul><li>They stayed at a friend&#x27;s beach house and enjoyed ten days of peace and seclusion.</li><li>Bonnie Hanssen has been in seclusion since the arrest of her husband.</li><li>He is drugged and placed in seclusion.</li><li>Milosevic, who has remained in seclusion for the past two weeks, has yet to make any public pronouncement.</li><li>The thing that drove him into seclusion was his failure to find anywhere a return of the warmth that flowed from him.</li><li>Apart from the seclusion and pressure of being watched under a gun, they all seemed in good spirits.</li></ul></section><section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">in seclusion</div><ul><li>The victim&#x27;s family has remained in seclusion since the shooting.</li></ul></section>
