- DefinitionsHTML: <section class="pos-block"><div class="pos-title">verb <span class="homnum">1</span></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">1</span><div class="def-en">to get or achieve something that will be permanent, especially after a lot of effort</div><div class="def-cn">〔尤指经过大量努力〕获得，得到</div><div class="patterns"><span class="label">Pattern</span> secure a deal/contract</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">Boyd’s goal secured his team’s place in the Cup Final.</div><div class="example-cn">博伊德的进球确保了球队进入足总杯决赛。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">The company secured a $20 million contract.</div><div class="example-cn">这家公司争取到了一份 2,000 万美金的合同。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">Negotiators are still working to secure the hostages’ release.</div><div class="example-cn">谈判人员仍在努力争取人质获释。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">Redgrave won his third Olympic gold medal, and secured his place in history.</div><div class="example-cn">雷德格雷夫赢得了个人第三枚奥运会金牌，使自己的名字载入了史册。</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">2</span><div class="def-en">to make something safe from being attacked, harmed, or lost</div><div class="def-cn">使安全，保护</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">Troops were sent to secure the border.</div><div class="example-cn">军队被派去保卫边境。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">They built a ten-foot high fence to secure the house against intruders.</div><div class="example-cn">他们筑了一道十英尺高的围栏，防止人闯入房子。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">an agreement to secure the future of the rainforest</div><div class="example-cn">一份保护热带雨林未来的协议</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">3</span><div class="def-en">to fasten or tie something firmly in a particular position</div><div class="def-cn">缚牢，系紧，将〔某物〕固定</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">John secured the boat firmly to the jetty.</div><div class="example-cn">约翰把小船牢牢系泊在码头。</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">4</span><div class="def-en">if you secure a debt or a loan, you legally promise that, if you cannot pay back the money you have borrowed, you will give the lender goods or property of the same value instead</div><div class="def-cn">为〔债务或贷款〕作抵押</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">He used his house to secure the loan.</div><div class="example-cn">他用自己的房子作抵押贷到了这笔钱。</div></div></div></section><section class="pos-block"><div class="pos-title">adjective <span class="homnum">2</span> <span class="pron">/sɪˈkʊə/</span></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">1</span><div class="activator">DEPEND ON/RELY ON</div><div class="def-en">a situation that is secure is one that you can depend on because it is not likely to change</div><div class="def-cn">稳固的，可靠的，稳定的</div><div class="relations">OPP insecure</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">There are no secure jobs these days.</div><div class="example-cn">如今已经没有铁饭碗了。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">We want a secure future for our children.</div><div class="example-cn">我们希望我们的孩子未来生活无虞。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">United’s position at the top of the league seems relatively secure.</div><div class="example-cn">联队在联赛中的头名位置似乎相对稳固。</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">2</span><div class="activator">SAFE</div><div class="def-en">locked or guarded so that people cannot get in or out or steal anything</div><div class="def-cn">锁牢的，关紧的，牢固的</div><div class="example-cn">这房子不是很安全 —— 我们需要加几把新锁。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">Keep your passport in a secure place.</div><div class="example-cn">把你的护照放在安全的地方。</div></div><div 岁以下儿童需要进管教所。</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">3</span><div class="def-en">safe from and protected against damage or attack</div><div class="def-cn">安全的，受保护的</div><div class="patterns"><span class="label">Pattern</span> secure from</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">Companies can offer secure credit card transactions over the Internet.</div><div class="example-cn">公司可以提供安全的网上信用卡交易。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">These elephants are relatively secure from poachers.</div><div class="example-cn">这些大象相对比较安全，不太会受到偷猎者的威胁。</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">4</span><div class="activator">CONFIDENT</div><div class="def-en">feeling confident about yourself and your abilities</div><div class="def-cn">〔对自己和自己的能力〕有自信的</div><div class="relations">OPP insecure</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">We want our children to be secure and feel good confident and certain about a situation and not worried that it might change</div><div class="def-cn">感到有保障的，没有顾虑的</div><div class="relations">OPP insecure</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">Workers no longer feel secure about the future.</div><div class="example-cn">工人们对未来不再感到有保障。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">It was enough money to make us feel financially secure.</div><div class="example-cn">那笔钱足够使我们感到经济上有保障。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">We huddled together, secure in the knowledge that the rescue helicopter was on its way.</div><div class="example-cn">我们挤在一起，知道救援直升机已经在赶来的路上，因而感到放心了。</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">6</span><div class="activator">ATTACH</div><div class="def-en">firmly fastened or tied, and not likely to fall down</div><div class="def-cn">固定住的，系牢的，缚紧的</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">Are you sure that shelf is secure?</div><div class="example-cn">你肯定那个架子牢固吗？</div></div></div></section>

- DefinitionsHTML: <section class="pos-block"><div class="pos-title">adverb <span class="pron">/ˈseldəm/</span></div><div class="sense"><div class="phrase">rarely</div><div class="activator">RARELY</div><div class="def-en">very rarely or almost never</div><div class="def-cn">很少，罕见，不常</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">Karen had seldom seen him so angry.</div><div class="example-cn">卡伦很少见他这么生气过。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">Seldom have I read an article that was so full of lies.</div><div class="example-cn">我很少读到这样满纸谎言的文章。</div></div></div></section>

- CorpusHTML: <section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">simplicity</div><ul><li>Van Gogh was attracted to the beauty and simplicity of a common table or kitchen chair.</li><li>It is assumed for simplicity that all transactions are in cash.</li><li>For simplicity, we have also omitted the transfer function and its first derivative in order to amplify the weight change process.</li><li>There is no superfluous decoration in Shaker design, yet there is a powerful beauty in its functional simplicity.</li><li>The functional simplicity of the gym contrasts with the opulence of the marble floors, the paintings and the drapes.</li><li>In a 3- D action game, simplicity is the key.</li><li>The jacket follows the lines of the body with graceful simplicity.</li><li>The design was beautiful in its simplicity.</li><li>For the sake of simplicity, we will ignore seasonal changes in population.</li><li>In this way, theoretical simplicity is obtained at the cost of denying the very experiential basis of the theory.</li><li>Remember to always use simplicity in design and plant boldly in groups of two or three for a strong impact.</li><li>That&#x27;s why the vast majority of users are attracted to Microsoft Windows by its very simplicity.</li></ul></section>
- OriginHTML: <div class="origin">simplicity (1300-1400) Old French simplicité, from Latin, from simplex “ single, simple ”, from sim- (→ SIMPLE) + -plex “ multiplied by ”</div>

back.</li><li>Blood pressure and lumbago have left these shrimps - pink and puffed as a rowing eight, slumped over their needles.</li></ul></section><section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">slump</div><ul><li>The survey also found that the likeliest effect of downsizing is a slump in morale, which can reduce productivity and profits.</li><li>Smith is in the deepest batting slump of his eight-year career.</li><li>The economic slump has dried up the big-ticket multi-billion yen projects that the majors used to thrive on.</li><li>The economic slump was nowhere to be seen, but hairline recession was another thing.</li><li>During the long housing slump, several high-profile crime stories gave skittish buyers one more reason to avoid the Inner Mission.</li><li>One of their major concerns was the slump in wool prices.</li><li>The slump in the property market is making it difficult for people to sell their homes.</li><li>The slump in Intel dragged down other tech stocks.</li><li>The slump in profits has limited the scope for corporation tax offsets but economic recovery should help ease the problem.</li><li>The post-war slump sent the unemployment figures to twice the expected level.</li></ul></section><section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">slump in</div><ul><li>a slump in exports</li></ul></section><section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">in a slump</div><ul><li>Such an assumption is a plausible one: in booms unemployment is low and in slumps it is high.</li><li>Exactly the opposite would apply in a slump year.</li><li>The Dow is reaching new highs, but small-company stocks are in a slump.</li><li>Some would say that that is because of the recession, but we are in a slump rather than a recession.</li><li>An economy in a slump or depression is generally characterised by high demand-deficient unemployment of both labour and capital.</li><li>They will be the first to go in a slump.</li><li>So again we would predict that the measured apc would be higher in a slump year than in a boom year.</li><li>Woods does not believe he is in a slump.</li></ul></section>

class="phrase">in spite of something</div><div class="activator">ALTHOUGH</div><div class="def-en">without being affected or prevented by something</div><div class="def-cn">虽然；不顾；尽管 … （仍 … ）</div><div class="relations">SYN despite</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">We went out in spite of the rain.</div><div class="example-cn">尽管下着雨，我们还是出去了。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="sense-no">2</span><div class="activator">CRUEL</div><div class="def-en">a feeling of wanting to hurt or upset people, for example because you are jealous or think you have been unfairly treated</div><div class="def-cn">恶意；怨恨；坏心眼</div><div class="patterns"><span class="label">Pattern</span> pure/sheer spite</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">She broke it just out of spite.</div><div class="example-cn">她就是出于恶意把它打破的。</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">3</span><div class="phrase">in spite of yourself</div><div class="activator">ALTHOUGH</div><div class="def-en">if you do something in spite of yourself, you do it although you did not expect or intend to do it</div><div class="def-cn">不由自主地，身不由己地</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">The picture made her laugh in spite of herself.</div><div class="example-cn">这幅画让她忍俊不禁。</div></div></div></section><section class="pos-block"><div class="def-cn">故意与〔某人〕作对，恶意对待</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">The neighbours throw things over the garden wall just to spite us.</div><div - CorpusHTML: <section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">in spite of the fact that</div><ul><li>He refuses to marry her, in spite of the fact that he gave her a legal document stating his intention.</li><li>The payments were awarded to him in spite of the fact that he participated in the negotiation of the deal with VastNed.</li></ul></section><section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">in spite of yourself</div><ul><li>Almost in spite of himself, he did well at Latin.</li><li>I feel a stab of envy in spite of myself.</li><li>The picture made her laugh in spite of herself.</li><li>Angie responds in spite of herself when Cain flirts with her.</li><li>I went along to my session, and I was shaking in spite of myself.</li><li>I hurried home, my heart pounding and my hands trembling in spite of myself -I could not believe it.</li></ul></section><section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">spite</div><ul><li>Agelong Hindu cruelty to his unhappy brethren filled Ambedkar with anger and spite.</li><li>Gerald&#x27;s feelings of injustice turned to bitterness and spite.</li><li>Biblical movies usually wind up epic in scope in spite of every effort to keep them small.</li><li>In spite of his other fencing skills, Richie had never quite mastered the post hammer.</li><li>In spite of the furor the codicil caused, life went on much as before.</li><li>In spite of the vote for Clinton in 1992, it is that second personality that has been in the ascendant recently.</li><li>Sometimes the pirates would sink a boat out of spite for wasting their time.</li><li>She quit college and worked as a waitress out of spite towards her parents.</li><li>Ignore what Martin says. It&#x27;s pure spite.</li><li>This is not to say that spite, malice or dishonesty may not exist; they clearly can.</li></ul></section><section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">pure/sheer spite</div><ul><li>Or were they keeping me here out of sheer spite?</li><li>They wanted to peck you all over, out of sheer spite.</li></ul></section><section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">spite</div><ul><li>Now he&#x27;s asking to keep the dog just to spite his ex-wife.</li><li>Pretty belonged in this country to spite La Bruja.</li><li>To spite me, Edusha talked of him continually.</li><li>We can be cutting off our noses to spite our faces if dealers aren&#x27;t making enough money to carry on.</li><li>He lives just to get back in office to spite the people.</li></ul></section><section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">just to spite</div><ul><li>You know what he&#x27;s like... I wouldn&#x27;t put it past him to say yes just to spite me.</li><li>Disappointed protesters complained that the government had reformed the tax just to spite them.</li></ul></section>

commitment, and that put a strain on our marriage.</li><li>Some had been finding work a strain and early retirement came as a relief.</li><li>a back strain</li><li>A pure-bred strain of barley is required in the production of this whisky.</li><li>Both of the positive control strains adhered strongly to HEp-2 cells.</li><li>The legal fight has been an enormous strain on my wife.</li><li>As she strain.</li><li>A particularly hardy strain of the virus can make you ill for over a week.</li><li>Such efforts put heavy strains on the financial and human resources of the organization.</li><li>They also needed to determine the genetic sequence of the virus so that they could compare it with known herpes strains.</li><li>She had a busy week, and she&#x27;s under a lot of strain at the moment.</li><li>Asthma / bronchitis claims jump 75 %; sprains / strains are 34. 6 % higher.</li><li>He had trouble handling the strain of raising eight kids.</li><li>He could see the strain in her face as she told him what she was going through.</li><li>The strain of managing such a huge company became too much for Anita.</li><li>The strain was beginning to show in their friendship.</li><li>He is putting his body under unbelievable strain, which is fine when he is 26.</li></ul></section><section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">find... strain</div><ul><li>Others have found similar strains only in repeated samples from the same individual.</li><li>Even Lancaster found his patience strained when Douglas told him how to play his part.</li><li>She did not find Flora any strain on something</div><ul><li>The waiting also puts a strain on parents.</li><li>Lack of stock control Goods which can not be quickly used or sold but put strains on cash flow.</li><li>One neck exercise could damage the top of the spine while straight leg sit-ups could put strain on the back.</li><li>And the demand for vaccine has started to put a strain on supplies.</li><li>The problem is the vigorous shaking of the trunk puts a strain on the roots.</li><li>So I was there until Sean was seventeen months, which put a strain on all of us, I think.</li><li>Occupational therapists also can modify items to make it possible to use them without placing a strain on arthritic joints.</li></ul></section><section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">strain of</div><ul><li>a deadly class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">strain every nerve</div><ul><li>Vincent strained every nerve to turn himself into a draughtsman acceptable to the illustrated papers, and the strain showed.</li></ul></section><section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">not strain yourself</div><ul><li>Continually adepts are warned that they must not strain themselves or try to experience these unnatural things.</li></ul></section><section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">strain</div><ul><li>Sometimes he strained his head up towards the ceiling and his mouth moved as if he were trying to shout orders.</li><li>James strained his right knee playing football.</li><li>Righthander Robert Person was scheduled to start, but a strained left hamstring sustained over the weekend could delay his spring debut.</li><li>She carries a small but distinct belly, which is straining the red material of the skirt.</li><li>Strain the sauce through a class="corpus-title">strain your ears/eyes</div><ul><li>He stood tensed, straining his ears.</li><li>She spoke softly, directing her remarks exclusively at Karelius and Moreau, so that the others were - DefinitionsHTML: <section class="pos-block"><div class="pos-title">adverb <span class="pron">/ˈstrɪktli/</span></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">1</span><div class="activator">STRICT</div><div class="def-en">in a way that must be obeyed</div><div class="def-cn">严格地，严厉地</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">Alcohol is strictly forbidden on school premises.</div><div class="example-cn">校内严禁喝酒。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">The ban on hunting is not strictly enforced.</div><div class="example-cn">狩猎禁令并未严格执行。</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">2</span><div class="activator">EXACT</div><div class="def-en">exactly and completely</div><div class="def-cn">完全地；确切地</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">That isn’t strictly true.</div><div class="example-cn">那并不完全正确。</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">3</span><div class="phrase">strictly speaking</div><div class="activator">TRUE</div><div class="def-en">used to say that something is true if you are going to be very exact and correct about it</div><div class="def-cn">严格地说</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">Strictly speaking, spiders are not insects.</div><div class="example-cn">严格地说，蜘蛛不是昆虫。</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">4</span><div class="activator">ONLY</div><div class="def-en">only for a particular person, thing, or purpose and no one else</div><div class="def-cn">严格限定地；只限于 …</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">This is strictly between us. - CorpusHTML: <section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">strictly speaking</div><ul><li>Neither the input nor the output of a Turing machine can, strictly speaking, be an infinite decimal.</li><li>Not strictly speaking, because the wedding was in a register office, and you don&#x27;t have a best man.</li><li>It is, strictly speaking, conferred by the Constitution.</li><li>That, he said, was, strictly speaking, inconceivable.</li><li>However, strictly speaking it is not a number but a physical quantity with units of mol-1.</li><li>Where there is such an approved standard it is, strictly speaking not mandatory for the manufacturer to comply with it.</li><li>Strictly speaking, spiders are not insects, although most people think they are.</li><li>Neither is an inflection of the other, so strictly speaking their differing linguistic origin should dictate separate indices.</li><li>This was not strictly speaking true.</li></ul></section><section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">strictly</div><ul><li>The closing dates were strictly adhered to by the Office of Works.</li><li>He completely disregarded strictly enforced social conventions and religious restrictions in order to contact the outcasts of society.</li><li>Local driving regulations are strictly enforced.</li><li>I play the piano strictly for fun.</li><li>But Weaver&#x27;s unusually modern sensibilities mark this novel strictly for the tourist market.</li><li>Mrs Berzins, who remembered herself as a young woman, did not strictly forbid her to go.</li><li>The pentecostal faith strictly forbids drunkenness, carousing, and infidelity.</li><li>The immigration laws have been strictly implemented.</li><li>Some people objected, but it was all strictly legal.</li><li>Where lordship was strong, as in Paris, the degree of self-government was strictly limited.</li><li>A Sweeter Lazarus was better written than strictly necessary.</li><li>The work is strictly on a volunteer basis.</li><li>Martha and Joan kept strictly to their part of the house.</li></ul></section><section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">strictly forbidden</div><ul><li>You can&#x27;t smoke inside the hospital - it&#x27;s strictly forbidden.</li><li>Any social contact with Silly-Willie was strictly forbidden.</li><li>He had found the porter visiting the superintendent nurse in her room, a form of social exchange that was strictly forbidden.</li><li>Adam, as a child, had been strictly forbidden ever to go in there.</li><li>Short hair is strictly forbidden for me not only because of my culture, but because of my lesbianism.</li><li>In some cultures eye contact between men and women is strictly forbidden outside the immediate family.</li><li>Although we have been strictly forbidden to enter the shed, my sister and I spend a lot of time in here.</li><li>Best of all, though, were the books that we had been strictly forbidden to touch.</li></ul></section>

- DefinitionsHTML: <section class="pos-block"><div class="pos-title">adjective <span class="pron">/səˈfɪʃənt/</span> <span class="register">formal</span></div><div class="sense"><div class="phrase">enough</div><div class="activator">ENOUGH</div><div class="def-en">as much as is needed for a particular purpose</div><div class="def-cn">足够的，充足的</div><div class="patterns"><span class="label">Pattern</span> sufficient for</div><div class="relations">SYN enough · OPP insufficient</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">We can only prosecute if there is sufficient evidence.</div><div class="example-cn">有了足够的证据，我们才能提出起诉。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">Unauthorized absence is sufficient reason for dismissal.</div><div class="example-cn">旷工足以成为解雇的理由。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">We need sufficient time to deal with the problem.</div><div class="example-cn">我们需要足够的时间来处理这个问题。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">The money is not sufficient to cover everything that needs doing.</div><div class="example-cn">这些钱不足以支付所有要做的事情。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">The recipe is sufficient for six people.</div><div class="example-cn">这份食谱的量足够六个人吃。</div></div></div></section>
- CorpusHTML: <section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">sufficient</div><ul><li>However, with endowments and Isas, there is always the risk that investment returns will not be sufficient.</li><li>This is not true of all goods, but that it is true of a substantial part is sufficient.</li><li>It was decided that there was sufficient evidence to convict Marconi.</li><li>The money should be sufficient for one month&#x27;s travel.</li><li>Proof of sufficient funds is required for entrance into Namibia.</li><li>In fact, sufficient nuclei are always present in the atmosphere.</li><li>Macleod was attacked by both liberals and conservatives in the Legco for failing to provide sufficient tax concessions to middle income earners.</li><li>Give yourself sufficient time to get really stuck into your subject-matter.</li><li>Given sufficient time with other things remaining unchanged, prices and wages would eventually be adjusted and full employment may be restored.</li></ul></section><section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">sufficient to do something</div><ul><li>He added that rental income was sufficient to cover interest payments.</li><li>That would have been sufficient to deprive John Major of a majority and bring down his government.</li><li>I do not read these passages as stating that an unlawful demand which is enforceable is perse sufficient to found recovery.</li><li>Or will it be sufficient to include background material as appropriate?</li><li>It was sufficient to outweigh Mr Field&#x27;s 165 to 113 second-round victory in the individual members&#x27; section.</li><li>Three orientations by size of the collectivity may be sufficient to overcome this limitation.</li><li>Weight on the nose or in the cockpit will be sufficient to prevent the glider lifting.</li><li>Three open sprinklers were found to be sufficient to stop even the most rapidly developing fire.</li></ul></section>

- DefinitionsHTML: <section class="pos-block"><div class="pos-title">noun <span class="pron">/ˈtestəməni/</span></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">1</span><div class="def-en">a formal statement saying that something is true, especially one a witness makes in a court of law</div><div class="def-cn">〔法庭上的〕证词</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">Barker’s testimony is crucial to the prosecution’s case.</div><div class="example-cn">巴克的证词对控方的指控起到了关键作用。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">In his testimony, he denied that the company had ignored safety procedures.</div><div class="example-cn">他在证词中否认公司忽视了安全程序。</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">2</span><div class="activator">SHOW/BE A SIGN OF</div><div class="def-en">a fact or situation that shows or proves very clearly that something exists or is true</div><div class="def-cn">证据；证明</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">These results are a testimony to the coach’s skill and hard work.</div><div class="example-cn">这些成绩是教练的水平和辛勤工作的证明。</div></div></div></section>

- DefinitionsHTML: <section class="pos-block"><div class="pos-title">adjective <span class="pron">/ˈtɒpɪkəl/</span></div><div class="sense"><div class="activator">NOW</div><div class="def-en">a subject that is topical is interesting because it is important at the present time</div><div class="def-cn">热门话题的；当前受到关注的</div><div class="patterns"><span class="label">Pattern</span> topical subject/issue/theme etc</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">a new TV comedy dealing with topical issues</div><div class="example-cn">一部反映热门问题的新电视喜剧</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">topical jokes (= jokes about topical subjects)</div><div class="example-cn">时事笑话</div></div></div></section>
- CorpusHTML: <section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">topical</div><ul><li>The humour was topical and apt.</li><li>a topical anesthetic</li><li>It is possible, too, to capitalise on topical events, like holidays, Christmas etc.</li><li>In this chapter, we have opted for a topical format.</li><li>A useful activity is to pull together the governors of several neighbouring schools for training and updating on topical issues.</li><li>The editor thinks that if an article isn&#x27;t topical it isn&#x27;t worth publishing.</li><li>It&#x27;s an old story but it has a topical message.</li><li>Firstly, do not prescribe antibiotics if a non-antibiotic topical preparation will suffice.</li><li>He is known for recording topical songs about social issues.</li><li>In the 1970s, he recorded topical songs about Watergate and the Vietnam War.</li><li>The group on active treatment used 60% less topical steroid.</li><li>Against this background, the first book devoted exclusively to this exciting and topical subject should be a significant landmark.</li></ul></section><section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">topical subject/issue/theme etc</div><ul><li>A useful activity is to pull together the governors of several neighbouring schools for training and updating on topical issues.</li><li>Open Space To be considered for this slot, pieces should be 1,000 words in length and address a topical issue.</li><li>Sometimes the salience of certain power bases may shift with topical issues.</li><li>Written in a straight-forward way, this guide is the ideal introduction to a highly topical subject.</li><li>Injuries and fitness have been topical issues for some time now.</li><li>This explores historical discoveries and topical issues likely to appeal to pupils.</li><li>Against this background, the first book devoted exclusively to this exciting and topical subject should be a significant landmark.</li></ul></section>

- DefinitionsHTML: <section class="pos-block"><div class="pos-title">noun <span class="homnum">1</span> <span class="pron">/trænˈzɪʃən, -ˈsɪ-/</span></div><div class="sense"><div class="register">formal</div><div class="activator">CHANGE FROM ONE THING TO ANOTHER</div><div class="def-en">when something changes from one form or state to another</div><div class="def-cn">过渡；转变，变迁</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">the smooth transition from full-time work to full retirement</div><div class="example-cn">从全职工作到完全退休的顺利过渡</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">Making the transition from youth to adulthood can be very painful.</div><div class="example-cn">从青少年过渡到成年有时是一个非常痛苦的过程。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">a society that is in transition (= changing)</div><div class="example-cn">一个正在转型的社会</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">the period of transition to full democracy</div><div class="example-cn">向全面民主的过渡时期</div></div></div></section><section class="pos-block"><div class="pos-title">verb <span class="homnum">2</span></div><div class="sense"><div class="def-en">to change to a new state or start using something new</div><div class="def-cn">过渡；转变</div><div class="patterns"><span class="label">Pattern</span> transition to/into</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">He will transition to his new role next month.</div><div class="example-cn">下个月他将转换成新角色。</div></div></div></section>
- CorpusHTML: <section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">transition</div><ul><li>You need a better transition between the second and third paragraphs.</li><li>The textile industry is currently in transition.</li><li>It seems to have been a religion that was in transition, which may explain some startling contradictions or apparent contradictions.</li><li>The new system will be introduced gradually over a six month transition period.</li><li>Except for Aunt Pat, my transition to city life was a series of agonies.</li><li>Mid-1945 was an important period of transition for him.</li><li>It&#x27;s difficult for someone who&#x27;s been a stage actor to make the transition to television.</li><li>a scheme to help families making the transition from welfare to work</li><li>For most people, the transition from infection to overt illness takes from six to ten years.</li><li>I resolved that the transition should be a smooth one.</li><li>Where the transitions were more subtle, as in changing cultural conceptions among the literati, the Jesuits were less successful.</li><li>The transition is even more painful if interest rates happen to be rising at the time.</li><li>The transition from a communist system to a free market economy will be difficult.</li></ul></section><section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">transition from something to something</div><ul><li>Conran&#x27;s transition from manufacturing to retailing was a gradual process.</li><li>He made a successful transition from selling religion to selling cars.</li><li>Adjustment was difficult and the transition from a rural to an inner-city setting was hardest for women.</li><li>Joan found the transition from sanctuary to Tower wholly satisfactory.</li><li>The carrier system plays a major role in the first step in the transition from analog to digital capabilities.</li><li>The transition from dualism to monism is painful.</li></ul></section>

- WordFamily: <div class="word-family"><div class="wf-pos">noun</div> <span class="wf-word">transparency</span> <span class="wf-word">transparentness</span> <div class="wf-pos">adverb</div> <span class="wf-word">transparently</span> <div class="wf-pos">adjective</div> <span class="wf-word">transparent</span></div>
- DefinitionsHTML: <section class="pos-block"><div class="pos-title">adjective <span class="pron">/trænˈspærənt, -ˈspeər-/</span></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">1</span><div class="activator">SEE</div><div class="def-en">if something is transparent, you can see through it</div><div class="def-cn">透明的</div><div class="relations">SYN clear ·, → opaque ·, translucent</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">a transparent plastic container</div><div class="example-cn">透明的塑料容器</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">2</span><div class="register">formal</div><div class="activator">CLEAR/EASY TO UNDERSTAND</div><div class="def-en">language or information that is transparent is clear and easy to understand</div><div class="def-cn">〔语言或信息〕清楚易懂的</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">The way the system works will be transparent to the user.</div><div class="example-cn">这个系统的运行方式对使用者来说清楚易懂。</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">3</span><div class="activator">OBVIOUS</div><div class="def-en">a lie, excuse etc that is transparent does not deceive people</div><div class="def-cn">〔谎言、借口等〕易看穿的，易识破的</div></div></section>
- CorpusHTML: <section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">transparent</div><ul><li>The boys arms and hands were so thin they seemed almost transparent.</li><li>The plastic is transparent.</li><li>Dry-fry the onion and garlic in a non-stick pan until the onion is transparent.</li><li>The fading colours and yellowish transparent appearance are clear indications of iron chlorosis caused by deficiencies in iron and trace elements.</li><li>The moments when nature seems transparent are evanescent.</li><li>The wall was as transparent as glass, but it was as if it revealed only another wall of uniform greyness.</li><li>a thin transparent fabric</li><li>He was a visitor from another, undersea world; an innocent, transparent, perfectly gentle alien.</li><li>With thin washes and the more transparent pigments, colour differences between the white and tinted sheets will be more apparent.</li><li>The box has a transparent plastic lid so you can see what&#x27;s inside.</li></ul></section>
- OriginHTML: <div class="origin">transparent (1400-1500) Medieval Latin present participle of transparere “ to show through ”, from Latin parere “ to show ”</div>

- CorpusHTML: <section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">triumphant</div><ul><li>The camera shutter winked and the photographer looked up from it, up and away, across the harbor; triumphant.</li><li>In his fourteen years as a fancier he has converted a hobby into something of a triumphant campaign.</li><li>She wanted to be alone; to escape with her triumphant discovery.</li><li>As John Gardner has said, talent is one thing, while its triumphant expression is another.</li><li>Only when we are fully deployed are we capable of that triumphant expression.</li><li>Winning a ring would be the triumphant moment of his career.</li><li>Then one day she rang him with the triumphant news that she had finished.</li><li>the triumphant women&#x27;s gymnastics team</li></ul></section><section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">triumphant look/smile/expression etc</div><ul><li>Only when we are fully deployed are we capable of that triumphant expression.</li><li>This piece of information I gave him with a triumphant smile.</li><li>He gave her a knowing, triumphant look and softly closed the door behind him.</li><li>But there was a new, triumphant look in the small red eyes.</li><li>As John Gardner has said, talent is one thing, while its triumphant expression is another.</li><li>A triumphant smile lit his perspiring face as he strode along the corridor to the kitchen.</li><li>Allowing herself a small triumphant smile, she started the same process on the right boot.</li></ul></section><section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">emerged triumphant</div><ul><li>After several weeks of fevered indigestion and almost terminal flatulence Grom emerged triumphant.</li><li>Embassies tell us the system has emerged triumphant.</li><li>Instead, rockeries and crazy paving abound and, after much tender loving care, a lawn has emerged triumphant.</li><li>It was, however, the Right which emerged triumphant from the political crisis brought by defeat.</li></ul></section>

- DefinitionsHTML: <section class="pos-block"><div class="pos-title">verb <span class="pron">/ˌʌndəˈteɪk/</span> <span class="register">formal</span></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">1</span><div class="activator">PROMISE</div><div class="def-en">to accept that you are responsible for a piece of work, and start to do it</div><div class="def-cn">承担；着手做〔某事〕</div><div class="patterns"><span class="label">Pattern</span> undertake a task/a project/research/a study etc</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">Dr Johnson undertook the task of writing a comprehensive English dictionary.</div><div class="example-cn">约翰逊博士担负起编写一本综合性英语词典的工作。</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">2</span><div class="phrase">undertake to do something</div><div class="register">formal</div><div class="def-en">to promise or agree to do something</div><div class="def-cn">承诺做某事，答应做某事</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">He undertook to pay the money back in six months.</div><div class="example-cn">他保证在六个月之内还钱。</div></div></div></section>

- DefinitionsHTML: <section class="pos-block"><div class="pos-title">adjective <span class="pron">/ʌnˈfɪt/</span></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">1</span><div class="activator">FIT PERSON#</div><div class="def-en">not in a good physical condition</div><div class="def-cn">〔身体〕不健康的；健康状况不佳的</div><div class="relations">SYN out of shape</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">She never gets any exercise – she must be really unfit.</div><div class="example-cn">她从不锻炼 —— 身体一定很不好。</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">2</span><div class="activator">GOOD ENOUGH#</div><div class="def-en">not good enough to do something or to be used for a particular purpose</div><div class="def-cn">不合适的，不适宜的；不胜任的</div><div class="patterns"><span class="label">Pattern</span> unfit for</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">Jenkins is unfit for public office.</div><div class="example-cn">詹金斯不适合担任公职。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">The meat was declared unfit for human consumption (= not suitable to eat).</div><div class="example-cn">这种肉被宣布不宜食用。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">The house was unfit for human habitation (= not good enough to live in).</div><div class="example-cn">这房子不宜住人。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">Hubbard was declared mentally unfit to stand trial.</div><div class="example-cn">哈伯德被宣布精神状态不宜接受审判。</div></div></div></section>
- CorpusHTML: <section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">unfit</div><ul><li>Other charges include driving while disqualified, driving while unfit due to drink, without insurance and without a licence.</li><li>I realised how unfit I was when I tried to run up the stairs.</li><li>For the unfit individual, three times per week should be the maximum number of exercise sessions.</li><li>The survey shows that the typical 16-year-old is unfit, lazy, and probably plays no sports at all.</li><li>an unfit mother</li><li>He described her as unfit to be called a Catholic and certainly unfit for motherhood.</li><li>The aim was to remove persons who were unfit to be ministers of religion either because of incompetence or scandalous behaviour.</li><li>Finally, there is a group of patients who are considered mentally unfit to make decisions concerning themselves.</li><li>Sometimes the Senate would decree that the son of a deceased emperor was unfit to succeed his father.</li><li>The doctor had told her that she was unfit to travel, but she came home anyway.</li><li>Please say briefly why you are unfit to work.</li></ul></section><section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">mentally unfit</div><ul><li>What if the patient is mentally unfit or is a terminally ill minor?</li><li>But more alarmingly, a planned fraud trial was scrapped because Burke was deemed mentally unfit to appear in the dock.</li><li>The judge ruled that he was mentally unfit to be tried.</li><li>Finally, there is a group of patients who are considered mentally unfit to make decisions concerning themselves.</li><li>Her 80-year-old husband, Harry, had been declared mentally unfit to stand trial.</li></ul></section>

- WordFamily: <div class="word-family"><div class="wf-pos">noun</div> <span class="wf-word">verifiability</span> <span class="wf-word">verification</span> <span class="wf-word">verifier</span> <div class="wf-pos">adjective</div> <span class="wf-word">verifiable</span> <span class="wf-word">verificatory</span> <div class="wf-pos">verb</div> <span class="wf-word">verify</span></div>
- DefinitionsHTML: <section class="pos-block"><div class="pos-title">verb <span class="pron">/ˈverɪfaɪ/</span> <span class="register">formal</span></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">1</span><div class="activator">CHECK/MAKE SURE</div><div class="def-en">to discover whether something is correct or true</div><div class="def-cn">核对，核实</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">A computer program verifies that the system is working.</div><div class="example-cn">电脑程序可以核查系统是否在运行。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">American forces will remain to verify compliance with the treaty.</div><div class="example-cn">美军将继续驻留，核查条约是否得到遵守。</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">2</span><div class="activator">SAY/STATE</div><div class="def-en">to state that something is true</div><div class="def-cn">证明，证实</div><div class="relations">SYN confirm</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">His statement was verified by several witnesses.</div><div class="example-cn">他的说法得到了几位证人的证实。</div></div></div></section>
- UsageHTML: <section class="usage-box"><div class="usage-title">Register</div><div class="usage-en">In everyday English, people usually say check rather than verify:</div><div class="usage-cn">在日常英语中，人们通常说 check ，而不说 verify</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">Can I just check that I have spelt your name correctly.</div><div class="example-cn">我就核对一下是否拼对了你的姓名，好吗？</div></div></section>
- CorpusHTML: <section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">verify</div><ul><li>The influence of rehydration rate on germination of artificially dried seed has been also verified.</li><li>Doctors have verified that the injury was indeed work-related.</li><li>The reader should trace through these two cases graphically to verify the conclusions we have outlined.</li><li>You can verify the facts in the report by calling his office.</li><li>Accountants are working to verify the figures.</li><li>Edey said it could take a week to verify those reports.</li></ul></section><section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">verify that/whether</div><ul><li>Thus we have verified that a transformation to a frame in free fall is always possible. 6.7.</li><li>A week after being asked, the staff of the commission said it needed more time to verify that figure.</li><li>Please verify that there is sufficient disk quota and privilege to create a file in the supplied working directory.</li><li>The reader can verify that this optimal solution is.</li><li>In the past week they have begun to verify that weapons and mines have been removed from the former fighting zone.</li><li>The company has verified that your balance is now at zero and all the charges and fees have been straightened out.</li></ul></section>
- OriginHTML: <div class="origin">verify (1300-1400) Old French verifier, from Medieval Latin verificare, from Latin verus; → VERY 2</div>

- DefinitionsHTML: <section class="pos-block"><div class="pos-title">adjective <span class="pron">/ˈvɪvɪd/</span></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">1</span><div class="activator">REAL/NOT IMAGINARY</div><div class="def-en">vivid memories, dreams, descriptions etc are so clear that they seem real</div><div class="def-cn">〔记忆、梦境、描述等〕生动的，逼真的，清晰的</div><div class="relations">OPP vague</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">I’ve got vivid memories of that summer.</div><div class="example-cn">我对那年夏天记忆犹新。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">He had a vivid picture of her in his mind.</div><div class="example-cn">他的脑海中清晰地留着她的形象。</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">2</span><div class="phrase">vivid imagination</div><div class="activator">IMAGINE</div><div class="def-en">an ability to imagine unlikely situations very clearly</div><div class="def-cn">活跃的想象力</div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">3</span><div class="phrase">colour</div><div class="def-en">vivid colours or patterns are very bright</div><div class="def-cn">〔色彩、图案〕鲜艳的，鲜明的</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">his vivid blue eyes</div><div class="example-cn">他碧蓝的眼睛</div></div></div></section>
- CorpusHTML: <section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">vivid imagination</div><ul><li>Although he&#x27;d never been blessed with a particularly vivid imagination, Charlie saw it all in an instant.</li><li>Her vivid imagination created some one tall and slim, blonde and attractive.</li><li>Mark deployed his vivid imagination in a wild-child narrative to create a boy who hunts deer, bears, and birds.</li><li>With her vivid imagination, Melissa could visualise the scene and it sickened her.</li><li>The Yippies were armed with a vivid imagination to match their rhetoric.</li><li>Course Moira always has had a vivid imagination, you have to take what she says with a pinch of salt.</li></ul></section><section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">vivid</div><ul><li>The book gives a vivid account of the author&#x27;s journey through northern Africa.</li><li>Include details to make your story as vivid as possible.</li><li>The bright exposure of a vivid blue patch alarms the attacker and may save the lizard&#x27;s life.</li><li>a vivid blue sky</li><li>I loved listening to his vivid descriptions of life in Italy.</li><li>Yet decades earlier, readers had already gotten a vivid fictionalized look at the inner earth from another science-fiction author.</li><li>One of my most vivid memories is of my first day at school.</li><li>The drug can make people suffer hallucinations and vivid nightmares.</li><li>But along the way Alice Thomas Ellis creates an ironic and vivid portrait of London, brilliantly catching its degradation and waste.</li><li>a vivid red cape</li><li>She could see nothing except a vivid scarlet blur, the colour of a London bus.</li><li>Repeat the steps above, trying to make it even more vivid than it was last time.</li><li>a cloud of vivid yellow butterflies</li></ul></section>
- OriginHTML: <div class="origin">vivid (1600-1700) Latin vividus, from vivere “ to live ”</div>

- DefinitionsHTML: <section class="pos-block"><div class="pos-title">adverb <span class="pron">/ˈrɒŋli/</span></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">1</span><div class="activator">WRONG/INCORRECT</div><div class="def-en">not correctly or in a way that is not based on facts</div><div class="def-cn">不正确地；错误地</div><div class="relations">OPP rightly</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">Matthew was wrongly diagnosed as having a brain tumour.</div><div class="example-cn">马修被误诊有脑瘤。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">His name had been wrongly spelt.</div><div class="example-cn">他的名字被拼错了。</div></div></div><div class="sense"><span class="sense-no">2</span><div class="activator">UNFAIR</div><div class="def-en">in a way that is unfair or immoral</div><div class="def-cn">不公正地；不道德地</div><div class="relations">OPP rightly</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">Human rights organizations maintain that the men have been wrongly convicted.</div><div class="example-cn">人权组织坚称这些人被错判了。</div></div></div></section>
- CorpusHTML: <section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">wrongly</div><ul><li>They feel guilty - quite wrongly.</li><li>Perrin had wrongly assumed that he would not get caught.</li><li>His lawyer says he was entrapped by overzealous prosecutors who wrongly characterized campaign contributions as bribes.</li><li>Matthew was wrongly diagnosed as having a brain tumor.</li><li>But, rightly or wrongly, Eden&#x27;s tenure in Downing Street is remembered as a single-issue premiership.</li><li>In any event, the Richmond City Council has supported its determination that minorities have been wrongly excluded from local construction contracting.</li><li>Rightly or wrongly, it is the latter whom they regarded as the enemy during the war of 1982.</li><li>Sometimes our pictures are so inaccurate that we see a person wrongly or miss him altogether.</li><li>One imagines, probably quite wrongly, that the moon must be like the wilder areas of Sutherland.</li><li>If you accidentally reformat characters wrongly, undo the reformatting straight away.</li></ul></section>

- DefinitionsHTML: <section class="pos-block"><div class="pos-title">adjective <span class="pron">/ˈjʌŋɡə/</span></div><div class="sense"><div class="phrase">somebody the Younger</div><div class="register">old use</div><div class="activator">NAME OF A PERSON</div><div class="def-en">someone famous who lived in the past and had the same name as their mother or father</div><div class="def-cn">小 … 〔用于称呼与母亲或父亲同名的旧时名人〕</div><div class="relations">→ elder</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">William Pitt the Younger</div><div class="example-cn">小威廉 · 皮特</div></div></div></section>
- CorpusHTML: <section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">somebody the Younger</div><ul><li>Pliny the Younger</li></ul></section><section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">younger</div><ul><li>There is much about cricket today that disturbs all of riper years and many who are much younger.</li><li>At school, the younger children go home an hour before the rest.</li><li>They lack self-confidence and often choose to play with younger children whom they can dominate.</li><li>She knew the determined stamp of her younger daughter, but there was also a heavier tread.</li><li>Frequently our younger engineers had leisure activities involving strenuous physical activity.</li><li>He is the most influential of the younger French photographers.</li><li>A younger man, or a more aggressive one, might have accepted the need for confrontation.</li><li>For this reason, campaigners like Rifkin are necessary, and younger scientists especially have a reluctant admiration for him.</li><li>He says the younger Symington is both a director and an investor in Melones Internacional.</li><li>Suppleness helps to keep you looking younger too as you will be able to move and walk better in later years.</li></ul></section>

- Pronunciation: noun: /ziːl/
- POS: noun
- WordFamily: <div class="word-family"><div class="wf-pos">noun</div> <span class="wf-word">zealant</span> <span class="wf-word">zealot</span> <span class="wf-word">zealotism</span> <span class="wf-word">zealotry</span> <span class="wf-word">zeal</span> <span class="wf-word">zealousness</span> <div class="wf-pos">adjective</div> <span class="wf-word">zealful</span> <span class="wf-word">zealless</span> <span class="wf-word">zealous</span> <div class="wf-pos">adverb</div> <span class="wf-word">zealously</span></div>
- DefinitionsHTML: <section class="pos-block"><div class="pos-title">noun <span class="pron">/ziːl/</span></div><div class="sense"><div class="activator">ENTHUSIASTIC</div><div class="def-en">eagerness to do something, especially to achieve a particular religious or political aim</div><div class="def-cn">〔尤指实现宗教或政治目标的〕热情，热忱</div><div class="patterns"><span class="label">Pattern</span> religious/revolutionary/missionary etc zeal · zeal for</div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">He approached the job with missionary zeal.</div><div class="example-cn">他以极大的热忱对待这份工作。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">In their zeal to catch drug dealers, police have ignored citizens’ basic civil rights.</div><div class="example-cn">警方抓捕毒贩心切，却忽略了市民基本的公民权利。</div></div><div class="example"><div class="example-en">their zeal for privatization</div><div class="example-cn">他们对私有化的热情</div></div></div></section>
- CorpusHTML: <section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">zeal</div><ul><li>The party converted to the free market with a zeal that out-Thatchered Thatcher and out-Reaganed Reagan.</li><li>The scientific establishment can resist a new idea with such complacent zeal that even Joshua with his trumpets would have no effect.</li><li>The turnover trouble overshadowed the fact that the Matadors played with a rare amount of zeal.</li><li>Now we saw them very rarely, and they were not hunting with their previous zeal.</li><li>Some of these arguments were presented with quiet, scientific calm, and others with prophetic zeal.</li><li>In the 60s many people brought a quasi-religious zeal to their calling.</li><li>But their zeal as reporters often took precedence over their New Deal leanings.</li><li>In their zeal to catch drug dealers, police have ignored citizens &#x27; basic civil rights.</li></ul></section><section class="corpus-group"><div class="corpus-title">religious/revolutionary/missionary etc zeal</div><ul><li>A new bureaucracy, the darling of the administration that establishes it, has a missionary zeal about its function.</li><li>The eyes of Mr. Morrissey gleam with a missionary zeal that shames into submission the cringing doubts of those yet unconvinced.</li><li>Professor Papert deserves high marks for missionary zeal.</li><li>A small but destructive minority has turned from religious zeal to crime, or to insurrection against its own governments.</li><li>Inside, I was gripped, as I always was, by the intense atmosphere of revolutionary zeal.</li><li>But it is obvious that one relatively small peninsula can not contain this missionary zeal indefinitely.</li><li>Whatever the job at Disney, it was approached with missionary zeal.</li></ul></section>
- OriginHTML: <div class="origin">zeal (1300-1400) Late Latin zelus, from Greek zelos</div>
